open.title: CSS @import of a bare package specifier resolves in client builds but fails in SSR builds
open.body:
### Describe the bug

A CSS file containing `@import "tailwindcss";` builds fine in a client build and fails in an SSR
build. Same project, same files, same Vite — the only difference is the `--ssr` flag:

```
$ npx vite build                          ✓ built in 2.14s
$ npx vite build --ssr entry-server.js    ✗ [postcss] ENOENT: no such file or directory,
                                            open '<projectRoot>/tailwindcss'
```

The path in the error appears in no source file: it is the bare specifier resolved against the
project root.

**Vite's own `Unable to resolve \`@import "…"\`` message is never emitted** — zero occurrences in the
full `--debug` output. So the only symptom is an ENOENT naming a path nobody wrote, which points at
nothing.

Changing the import to `@import "tailwindcss/index.css";` makes the SSR build succeed.

Not submitting a PR.

### The resolver appears to report success on failure

`dist/node/chunks/node.js` (8.1.5):

1. `:22574` — `const needInlineImport = code.includes("@import");`
2. `:22580` — `if (needInlineImport) postcssPlugins.unshift(…)` — the bundled `postcss-import` goes to
   position 0, ahead of any user PostCSS plugin.
3. `:22584-22587` —
   ```js
   const resolved = await atImportResolvers.css(environment, id, atRule.source?.input.file);
   if (resolved) return path.resolve(resolved);
   if (!path.isAbsolute(id)) environment.logger.error(`Unable to resolve \`@import "${id}"\` …`);
   return id;
   ```
4. ENOENT on the resulting `<projectRoot>/tailwindcss`.

The error being logged **zero** times, together with an ENOENT naming `<projectRoot>/tailwindcss`,
seems jointly consistent only with `atImportResolvers.css` returning a truthy unresolved value — the
bare string itself — so the truthy branch is taken and the error branch is skipped. A falsy return
would have produced the clear message instead.

### The bare specifier is expected to resolve

The CSS resolver is configured for this case at `:22453-22465` — `extensions: [".css"]`,
`mainFields: ["style"]`, `conditions: ["style", …]`, `tryIndex: false` — and `tailwindcss@4.3.3`
declares `"style": "index.css"` and `exports["."].style = "./index.css"`, with
`node_modules/tailwindcss/index.css` present.

### Both explicit subpaths work, which localises it

```css
@import "tailwindcss/index.css";   /* SSR build succeeds */
@import "tailwindcss/index";       /* SSR build succeeds */
```

The extensionless form matters because `tryIndex: false` — it is not succeeding by index-guessing;
`./index` is an explicit key in the exports map. Both working forms name a literal key and need no
condition matching, while the failing bare form requires resolving `exports["."]` through the `style`
condition. So the failure looks specific to **conditional resolution of the package root**, in the
SSR environment only.

### Relationship to #22766 / #22775 — same call site, opposite branch, and the fix is already in

`#22766` ("Vite 8.1 doesn't resolve `tsconfigPaths` in CSS @import directives") is the nearest
existing report and is **not** this bug. Its own log shows three differences:

| | #22766 | this report |
|---|---|---|
| `Unable to resolve …` | **present** | **absent**, 0 matches under `--debug` |
| ENOENT path | `open '@/styles/imported.css'` — the raw specifier | `open '<root>/tailwindcss'` — `path.resolve` applied |
| Environment | `building client environment` | **SSR only**; the client build of the same project succeeds |

Those are the two branches of the same four lines. In #22766 the resolver returned **falsy**, so the
error branch ran, the message was logged, and `return id` handed postcss-import the raw specifier —
which is why their ENOENT names it unchanged. Here the resolver returns **truthy**, so
`path.resolve(resolved)` runs on an unresolved bare string and no message is logged — which is why
the ENOENT names a root-joined path instead. Their log shows what the falsy path looks like, and it
looks nothing like this.

**The fix for #22766 shipped and does not cover this.** `#22775` ("fix(css): resolve tsconfig paths
in CSS and Sass @import") merged 2026-06-30 and changed the importer passed to the resolver. That
change is present in the 8.1.5 build used here — `:22584` reads
`atImportResolvers.css(environment, id, atRule.source?.input.file)`, the fixed form. 8.1.5 was
published 2026-07-16.

So this is not a case the importer fix missed by timing; it is an adjacent failure mode at the same
call site that the fix does not address, because it turns on conditional resolution of a package root
rather than on tsconfig ownership of the importer.

`#22837` and `#23052` are also open against CSS `@import` resolution after the 8.1 change, and are
likewise distinct from this case.

### Version boundary

Vite 7.3.3 builds the same project. 8.1.5 fails. The failure path is unchanged in 8.2.0-beta.0 —
`needInlineImport` at `:23055`, the `unshift` at `:23061`, the identical resolve callback at
`:23065-23068`, and `createCSSResolvers` with the same options at `:22934-22943`; only line numbers
shift.

Vite 8.1 moved CSS resolution to `oxc-resolver`, which is a plausible origin. **`oxc-resolver` ships
inside rolldown, and I did not diff rolldown** — so this identifies where the failure surfaces in
Vite's call path, not its final home.

### Scope

Tested with `tailwindcss` only. The mechanism is not obviously specific to it — it turns on resolving
a package root through an exports condition — but I have not verified another package, so Tailwind
should be read as the example I measured rather than as the boundary of the bug.

Also reproduces through Nuxt 4.5.1, where the client environment builds and emits CSS and the SSR
environment fails identically. That is what led here; the reproduction below removes the framework
entirely.

### Workaround

`@import "tailwindcss/index.css";` — output verified equivalent to the Vite 7 build.

### Reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/wnh9c8

### Steps to reproduce

Six

open.title: Support `?inline` on an HTML `<script src>` to emit the bundled entry inline
open.body:
### Description

Some scripts are only correct if they run **before** other resources — they cannot be a file request or a deferred module. Today these have to be hand-written inline in `index.html`, which makes them the only code in an otherwise fully typed project that is untranspiled, unlinted, and unable to import shared constants.

Concrete use cases:

- **Consent Mode / analytics bootstrapping** — consent defaults must be registered before the tag loader initializes, or the first hits fire under an undeclared state. This is a compliance requirement, not a preference.
- **Theme / no-FOUC scripts** that must run before first paint.
- **Feature detection** that sets classes the CSS depends on.
- **Early error handlers** that need to catch bundle load failures.

Nothing currently covers this. `vite-ignore` skips the script entirely, so a `.ts` source is never transpiled. `build.assetsInlineLimit` applies to imported assets, not entry scripts. `?inline` exists only in `css.ts` (`inlineRE`) with no JS equivalent. `inlineEntryChunk` in `html.ts` only elides an entry that `isEntirelyImport` — it removes an indirection chunk, it never writes code into the document. `toScriptTag` always emits `<script src=…>`.

### Suggested solution

In theory the HTML plugin already has all the pieces: it parses script attributes, collects module entries as build inputs, and disposes of chunks it has decided not to reference. An `?inline` query could be recognised at parse time and carried through so that, at bundle generation, the entry's code is written into the document instead of being referenced by a tag — the chunk then being discarded the same way an entirely-import entry already is.

The two open questions are what happens to the entry's imported chunks, and the output format. An inline `type="module"` is still deferred, so the emitted script would have to be a plain IIFE — otherwise the feature would appear to work while missing the point.

### Alternative

A `transformIndexHtml` hook that runs a nested `build()` in lib/IIFE mode with `write: false` and substitutes the output for a placeholder comment. This works and is what we ship today, but it means a second bundler invocation per HTML transform, and the placeholder is a magic string with no compile-time guarantee — a missing one silently produces a page with the script absent unless you add your own check.

`vite-plugin-singlefile` solves the adjacent problem (inline everything for single-file distribution) but is far too coarse for one order-critical entry.

Keeping the script hand-written inline in `index.html` — the status quo everywhere — avoids all tooling but leaves it untranspiled, unlinted, and unable to share constants with the rest of the source.

### Additional context

open.title: agent-friendly dev/preview server mode
open.body:
### Description

Writing code with agents is a great experience with Vite... right up until the agent wants to use the dev server. Because of how a dev server works (long-running execution, pretty-looking logs printed as they come in, etc), agents have trouble working with dev servers, either spawning dev servers without shutting them down first which consequently slows down the user's machine and stealing resources or the agent becomes completely frozen until the user manually intervenes and shuts down the command line for them. Not exactly great.

### Suggested solution

The Astro team have also seen this behaviour with their triaging AI agent, as they note in the [Astro 7 release post, talking about their new background dev server](https://astro.build/blog/astro-7/#background-dev-server). Their new background dev server ensures the agent doesn't trip up on dev servers by being more agent-friendly:

- command line only blocks until the dev server is ready
- the command line prints simplified dev commands the agent can use that also follow this philosophy
- the existing instance is recorded on disk and returned to the agent when they try to start another dev server

I think something similar could work for Vite (and be adoptable for tools that build on top like Vitest watch mode).

If desired, this philosophy can also be extended down to the Rolldown layer and replicated into tsdown, although that will be its own separate issue on their respective repositories.

### Alternative

There are probably other agent-friendly dev server setups that could work here, one that I came up with is using simply not recording the lockfile and somehow checking for an existing PID running Vite. This has some advantages and disadvantages over the solution mentioned above, but it is a solution that may be worth considering.

Alongside this, there can potentially also be a slightly tweaked implementation for Vite, compared to Astro. For example, the agent might be able to `curl` a special endpoint to trigger commands instead of using the CLI, or maybe Vite outputs plaintext/markdown logs instead of JSON.

### Additional context

Even if the Vite dev server doesn't become more agent-friendly, the lockfile feature alone could be helpful in case a human (like me late at night) forgets they already have a dev server up and transforming. It would also be friendly for scripts and other stuff to build around. Additionally, I think the preview server and dev server can coexist independently, and maybe a warning could pop up if, say, a dev server is already running but the user is spawning a preview server. The rational is that the preview server is serving pre-compiled output that may be what the user is wanting to reference when modifying the code, which would then be displayed by the dev server.

open.title: CSS @import resolution ignores user resolveId plugins, leaving resolve.alias.customResolver (now deprecated) as the only way to customize CSS import resolution
open.body:
### Description

The deprecation of customResolver assumes plugins are an equivalent replacement — but for CSS @import they are not, so the deprecation currently has no viable migration path.

Vite 8 deprecates resolve.alias entries that use customResolver (warned from resolveResolveOptions). The suggested replacement is a plugin resolveId hook. However, CSS @import resolution never runs user plugins, so customResolver is the only mechanism able to customize how CSS imports are resolved. Following the deprecation guidance breaks CSS resolution.

This affects any setup that needs programmatic/conditional resolution of CSS @import specifiers (multi-layer frameworks, monorepos, virtual layer aliases, "first existing file wins" resolution, etc.).

**Minimal repro:**

Add a resolve.alias entry with a customResolver that maps ~layers/foo.css → an existing file. It works, but logs the deprecation warning.
Remove customResolver; instead register a plugin with an enforce: 'pre' resolveId hook that resolves the same specifier. In a .js/.vue file the import resolves; in a CSS @import (especially a nested one) it fails with ENOENT.

### Suggested solution

Either:

(A) CSS @import resolution consults user resolveId hooks (or a documented CSS-resolution hook), giving the deprecation a real migration path; or
(B) customResolver on resolve.alias is not deprecated for the CSS-resolution case until an equivalent plugin API exists; or
(C) a documented, supported API to inject a custom CSS @import resolver (e.g. css.resolve / a resolver hook honored by both the PostCSS and Lightning CSS paths).

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

Real-world use case: a layered Nuxt framework resolving ~layers/** across multiple filesystem roots ("first existing file wins"), which requires programmatic resolution for both JS and CSS imports. The plugin resolveId path covers JS/Vue/SSR/virtual modules perfectly; only CSS @import still forces customResolver.

open.title: Tracking: playground tests skipped under bundled dev mode
open.body:
This issue tracks every playground test that is skipped under bundled dev mode (`experimental.bundledDev`). The goal is to shrink the list to zero.

## How the suite runs

The test infra landed in #23027.

- Command: `pnpm run test-serve-bundled`. It runs the whole playground e2e suite with `experimental.bundledDev` forced on for every playground (env var `VITE_TEST_BUNDLED_DEV=1`, no per-playground config changes).
- CI runs it as the `Test serve (bundled dev)` step.

A test that does not pass yet is skipped in one of two ways:

- Most cases in the file fail → the whole spec file is listed in `bundledDevExclude` in `vitest.config.e2e.ts`.
- Only a few cases fail → the file stays enabled, and each failing case is marked `test.skipIf(isBundledDev)` or `describe.skipIf(isBundledDev)` (`isBundledDev` comes from `~utils`).

The skipped tests still run in normal serve and build modes.

To close a skip: fix the behavior, or decide that the bundled-dev behavior is correct and update the assertion. Then remove the skip.

**Harness note:** until the first bundle is ready, bundled dev serves a fallback page that reloads itself. `vitestSetup.ts` waits for the real page after `page.goto`, with a 15s limit so a playground whose first bundle fails on purpose still runs (`hmr-full-bundle-mode` is exempt — it asserts the fallback page itself). Without this wait, test results depend on timing.

## Baseline numbers

From the baseline run on `main` @ `34af7b7` (2026-07-23, freshly built dist):

- **495 failing tests + 2 crashing suites in 47 spec files** (out of 1284 tests in 108 files).
- 531 tests skip only under bundled dev: the 497 baseline failures, documented over-skips in shared helpers, and 5 more found while stabilizing the suite (3× `should have no 404s` in assets / chunk-importmap / legacy, `css > css import from js`, `hmr > CSS HMR with this.addWatchFile`).
- Two `backend-integration` tests skip only on Windows under bundled dev.

## Why most of them fail

In bundled dev, the server serves the output of a rolldown bundle from memory. It does not serve single source files by URL the way normal dev does. Most failures come from that one difference. Minimal example — same import, different URL:

```js
import imgUrl from './nested/asset.png'
// normal dev:  '/nested/asset.png'          (read from disk, transformed on request)
// bundled dev: '/assets/asset-C1hss4aq.png' (bundle output, served from memory)
```

A URL that is not a bundle output has no handler: the server answers 404 or falls back to the HTML page. This also means the `fs.allow` / `fs.deny` checks never run — a denied file returns 404 or the fallback page instead of 403.

## Failure classes

| # | class | playgrounds (skips) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Asset URLs are bundle-output paths, not source paths | assets (122), assets-sanitize (2), html (16, partly), css (14, partly) | The tests expect dev-style source-path URLs. Decision needed: keep source-path URLs in bundled dev, or accept hashed URLs and update the assertions. |
| 2 | Only bundle outputs are served: static and `/@fs/` URLs return 404; `fs.allow`/`fs.deny` answers 404 or the fallback page instead of 403 | fs-serve (108) | Verified safe: denied files are never served, and no content leaks. But fetches of allowed files also return 404, so apps that `fetch()` files inside `fs.allow` break. Needs a static-file + fs-check middleware behind the bundle lookup. |
| 3 | HMR gaps | hmr (42, incl. 2 crashing `acceptExports` suites), hmr-ssr (1) | Owned by the HMR redesign work. |
| 4 | Workers | worker (50) | Worker bundling works differently under bundled dev (iife worker bundles, no HMR client inside workers). |
| 5 | Dep optimizer interplay | optimize-deps (51), optimize-deps-no-discovery (1) | Timeouts and empty pages. The optimizer's URLs and metadata do not match how bundled dev serves files. |
| 6 | Sourcemaps | css-sourcemap (16, incl. 3 lightningcss snapshot mismatches), js-sourcemap (9) | Includes serving sourcemaps for lazy chunks. |
| 7 | Import-map / CSP / misc long tail | chunk-importmap (9), csp (5), tailwind (4), resolve (4), dynamic-import (4), css-lightningcss (4), backend-integration (4), tailwind-v3 (3), legacy (3), glob-import (3), forward-console (3), css-codesplit (3), tsconfig-json-load-error (2), transform-plugin (2), json (2), environment-react-ssr (2), env (2), wasm (1), tsconfig-json (1), object-hooks (1), module-graph (1), extensions (1), css-no-codesplit (1), css-lightningcss-root (1) | Most of these follow from classes 1–2 (URL shapes, files not served), plus small per-feature gaps. Un-skip a test to see its current error. |

## How to work on one skip

1. Remove the spec file from `bundledDevExclude` in `vitest.config.e2e.ts`. If the file is already enabled and only a few cases fail, remove the `skipIf(isBundledDev)` from those cases instead.
2. Run just that playground: `pnpm run test-serve-bundled <playground-name>`.
3. Fix the behavior, or update the assertion if the bundled-dev behavior is the intended one. Keep the file enabled.

## Checklist (per playground)

The live checklist is kept in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/23028#issuecomment-5190734145 and is updated as work lands.

open.author: sapphi-red

open.title: bundledDev: server-side API to map module id to served URL (needed for SSR modulepreload/hydration hints)
open.body:
### Description

SSR frameworks that stream HTML serialize **per-module URLs into the document itself**, ahead of any client code:

- `<link rel="modulepreload" href="...">` hints, so the browser fetches lazy route chunks in parallel with the entry bundle during HTML parse, and
- a hydration module map (e.g. `_$HY.r["…_assets"] = { hydrationKey: url }`) written by inline `<script>` chunks in the stream, which the client runtime `import()`s **before** resuming server-rendered DOM.

Concrete case: SolidStart on solid-js 2.0 / vite-plugin-solid. In (unbundled) dev, the framework's asset resolver answers "what URL serves module X?" by identity — the module's dev URL, e.g.:

```
/src/routes/(basic).tsx?pick=default&pick=$css
```

Under `experimental.bundledDev` (Vite 8.1) that contract breaks:

- The served HTML (200) still contains those source-path URLs in the modulepreload hints and the hydration module map — the SSR side has nothing else to emit.
- Requesting the URL itself returns **404**: only bundled output files are served (`memoryFilesMiddleware` looks up `memoryFiles.get(pathname.slice(1))` and falls through for anything that isn't an output `fileName`).
- The client runtime's pre-hydration `import(url)` therefore rejects, hydration falls back to a fresh client render, and the page ends up with duplicated DOM. In SolidStart's test app this is 18 failing e2e specs (`apps/tests` `e2e:bundled-dev`) that all pass in normal dev.

The underlying gap: a server-side plugin has **no API to translate a module id into its served URL** in bundled dev.

- `BundledDev.memoryFiles` maps output `fileName → { source, etag }`. There is no facade/module-id → fileName mapping exposed, so you can't go from `src/routes/(basic).tsx?pick=default&pick=$css` to `assets/_basic_-DhY….js`.
- The lazy-compile endpoint `/@vite/lazy?id=…&clientId=…` (`triggerLazyBundlingMiddleware` → `devEngine.compileEntry(moduleId, clientId)`) requires a **live HMR clientId** and returns compiled *code*, not a URL — unusable from an SSR render pass that must emit URLs into HTML before any client connects.

Put differently: in normal dev, module → URL is answerable by identity (the URL *is* the module path); in production builds it's answerable via `manifest.json`. Bundled dev is currently the only topology that provides neither.

We want to stress this is a **correctness requirement for streamed SSR hydration in bundled dev, not an optimization**: the URLs are fixed server-side and shipped in the HTML before any client code executes, so there is no client-side recovery — either the server can emit servable URLs or hydration of code-split routes fails. We understand `bundledDev` is experimental and evolving; if there's an intended pattern for this that we've missed, pointers welcome, and we're glad to help test an API.

### Suggested solution

A stable server-side API — on the client `Environment` or the dev server — that, under `bundledDev`, maps **module id → served URL(s)** (the entry chunk for that module, ideally with its static import chain for complete preload hints), e.g.:

```ts
const urls = await server.environments.client.bundledDev.resolveModuleUrl(
  "src/routes/(basic).tsx?pick=default&pick=$css"
);
// → ["/assets/_basic_-DhYx12ab.js", ...]
```

Semantics we'd need: awaits the current build if one is in flight (like `waitForInitialBuildFinish`), and reflects lazy-compiled entries once they exist (or triggers compilation without requiring a browser clientId).

### Alternative

For the **client entry** specifically, SolidStart already works around this by hardcoding the served path, `assets/${basename(entry)}.js`, which is only possible because the entry's `entryFileNames` is predictable. Hashed lazy route chunks have no equivalent workaround — their served names are only knowable from the bundle graph Vite holds. Emulating a manifest by watching `memoryFiles` doesn't work either, since there's no exposed mapping from output files back to the facade module ids the framework knows about.

### Additional context

Reproduction:

The HTML streams fine; the module request 404s; anything gated on it fails — while the same URL works in unbundled dev.

open.title: Add a "copy error" button to the dev server error overlay
open.body:
### Description

## Description

When Vite's error overlay shows a build/transform error, there's currently 
no quick way to copy the full error details (plugin name, message, file 
location, code frame, stack trace) as plain text.

This makes it slower to:
- Paste errors into AI coding assistants for debugging help
- File clear bug reports (for Vite itself or upstream plugins)
- Share the exact error with a teammate over Slack/Discord

## Suggested solution

Add a small "Copy Error" button to the overlay (e.g. top-right corner of 
the window) that copies a formatted plain-text version of the error to 
the clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`.

## Alternative considered

Users can already select-and-copy the overlay text manually, but the 
stack trace often has scrollable overflow that makes full manual 
selection unreliable, and combining it with the plugin/message/file 
lines requires several separate selections.

I have a working implementation and I'm happy to open a PR if this 
sounds good.

### Suggested solution

In `packages/vite/src/client/overlay.ts`, add a small "Copy Error" button 
to the error overlay's template (near the top-right of the `.window` 
container). On click, it would build a formatted plain-text string from 
the same data already rendered in the overlay — plugin name, message, 
file location, code frame, and stack trace — and copy it to the 
clipboard via `navigator.clipboard.writeText()`.

I have a working local implementation and I'm happy to open a PR.

### Alternative

Users can already select-and-copy the overlay text manually, but the 
stack trace section has scrollable overflow, which makes full manual 
selection unreliable. Combining the plugin/message/file/stack into one 
clean copy currently requires several separate manual selections.

### Additional context

Use case: pasting the full error into AI coding assistants, filing clear 
bug reports, or sharing with teammates over Slack/Discord — all faster 
with one click than manual selection across multiple overlay sections.

open.title: `buildStart` runs twice when the client module graph is accessed in bundled dev
open.body:
### Describe the bug

With bundled dev enabled, client plugins can receive two `buildStart` calls for the same initial build.

Rolldown runs the plugin lifecycle while creating the client bundle. Vite’s regular client plugin container still considers itself unstarted, so the first module graph lookup starts the same plugins again.

This came up in TanStack Start while collecting CSS for an SSR response. Vite injects bundled-dev CSS after the client JavaScript runs, but Start still needs to provide CSS in the initial SSR HTML. Looking up those CSS modules through the client module graph triggers the second `buildStart`.

Plugins that keep build-scoped state can lose or reset state created during the actual bundle.

```sh
pnpm dev
```

Then, in another terminal run:
```sh
curl http://localhost:5173/__repro
```

open.title: CSS Modules: string `generateScopedName` pattern produces different class names for the same file when imported with a query (e.g. `?inline`)
open.body:
### Describe the bug

When `css.modules.generateScopedName` is a **string pattern** containing `[hash]`, the hash is computed from the full module id **including the import query**.

`runPostCSS` passes `from: removeDirectQuery(id)` to postcss ([css.ts](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts#L1732-L1739)) — only `?direct` is stripped, any other query stays. For string patterns `postcss-modules` delegates to `generic-names`, which hashes `path.relative(process.cwd(), filepath) + '\0' + localName`, where `filepath` still carries the query.

As a result, the same class in the same file gets **different scoped names within a single build**, depending on how the module was imported:

```js
import styles from './foo.module.css'          // .title -> _SGzINF8r
import inline from './foo.module.css?inline'   // .title -> _ZhC-jWQM
```

The default (function) generator of postcss-modules hashes the CSS content, so it is not affected — only string patterns are.

**Real-world impact:** Nuxt's `inlineStyles` feature imports every style with `?inline&used` ([ssr-styles plugin](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/main/packages/vite/src/plugins/ssr-styles.ts)). With a string `generateScopedName` pattern, the CSS inlined into the SSR response gets different class names than the server-rendered markup and the client bundle, so the page renders unstyled until the external CSS loads. This is how we hit it in production.

**Possible fix**: convert string patterns to a function inside Vite, passing a cleaned filename:

```ts
// packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts, compilePostCSS
if (typeof modulesOptions.generateScopedName === 'string') {
  const generate = genericNames(modulesOptions.generateScopedName, { context: config.root })
  modulesOptions = {
    ...modulesOptions,
    generateScopedName: (name, filename) => generate(name, cleanUrl(filename)),
  }
}
```

This would also make the hash independent of `process.cwd()` (`generic-names` currently uses cwd as the hashing context, so the same project produces different class names when the build runs from a different directory).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/andreyshivas/vite-css-modules-query-hash-repro

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm run check   # vite build + compares the scoped names from both imports
```

Output:

```
scoped name via normal import:  _SGzINF8r
scoped name via ?inline import: _ZhC-jWQM

BUG: same file + same class produced two different scoped names in one build
```

Reproduced on vite 7.3.1 and 8.1.5.

### System Info

open.title: Allow frameworks to customise or suppress ModuleRunner full-reload error logging
open.body:
### Description

I’m the author of `vite-plugin-html-pages`, a framework-like Vite plugin that evaluates page modules during development using Vite’s SSR environment:

```js
await server.environments.ssr.runner.import('/src/index.ht.js');
```

When a page contains an error, for example:

```js
import { html } from 'javascript-to-html';

export default () =>
  html(
    header(), // ReferenceError: header is not defined
  );
```

the plugin catches the error so it can:

- keep the development server running;
- display a concise, framework-specific diagnostic;
- allow the developer to fix the file and continue without restarting Vite.

For example:

```text
[vite-plugin-html-pages] Page reload failed — watching for file changes...
```

The initial `runner.import()` rejection can be handled by the plugin.

However, once the module has loaded successfully, later source changes can cause ModuleRunner to automatically re-import its registered entry points during a full reload. If that automatic re-import fails, Vite logs the error directly:

```text
[vite] (ssr) page reload src/index.ht.js
[vite] (ssr) program reload
[vite] (ssr) An error happened during full reload
header is not defined
ReferenceError: header is not defined
    at ...
```

The plugin subsequently receives or handles the failed page reload and prints its own diagnostic, resulting in duplicate error output.

This means framework authors cannot fully control the presentation of recoverable full-reload errors, even when their framework intentionally keeps running and provides its own error reporting.

### Current behaviour

A framework initially imports an entry point:

```js
await server.environments.ssr.runner.import('/src/index.ht.js');
```

After that module has loaded successfully, editing it so that evaluation fails causes ModuleRunner’s automatic full-reload process to produce:

```text
[vite] (ssr) page reload src/index.ht.js
[vite] (ssr) program reload
[vite] (ssr) An error happened during full reload

ReferenceError: header is not defined
    ...
```

The framework then also reports its recoverable error:

```text
[vite-plugin-html-pages] Page reload failed — watching for file changes...
```

The framework currently has no supported way to suppress, replace, or customise the error emitted by ModuleRunner’s automatic full-reload path.

### Suggested solution

Provide a way for framework authors to control error logging for automatic ModuleRunner reloads.

For example, this could be configured when creating or accessing the runnable environment:

```js
{
  runner: {
    logReloadErrors: false,
  },
}
```

Alternatively, `runner.import()` could accept an option that also applies to automatic re-imports of the registered entry point:

```js
await server.environments.ssr.runner.import(id, {
  logErrors: false,
});
```

Another possibility would be an error callback:

```js
{
  runner: {
    onReloadError(error, context) {
      // Return true if the error has been handled by the framework.
      return true;
    },
  },
}
```

The reload would still fail and the relevant promise or callback would still expose the error, but Vite would not print its default terminal output when the framework has opted to handle it.

The default behaviour could remain unchanged.

### Why this would be useful

Frameworks increasingly use the Environment API and ModuleRunner to implement their own development workflows.

Recoverable evaluation failures are normal while editing source files. Frameworks may want to provide:

- concise error messages;
- source frames;
- framework-specific guidance;
- browser overlays;
- reassurance that the development server is still running.

Allowing frameworks to customise or suppress ModuleRunner’s automatic full-reload error output would avoid duplicate diagnostics and enable a more polished developer experience without changing Vite’s default behaviour.

### Additional context

The logging does not appear to come directly from the initial explicit `runner.import()` call.

It occurs when a previously imported entry point is automatically re-imported after an HMR/full-reload event:

```text
[vite] (ssr) program reload
[vite] (ssr) An error happened during full reload
```

I can provide a minimal reproduction that:

1. imports a module with `server.environments.ssr.runner.import()`;
2. lets it load successfully;
3. edits a dependency so that evaluation fails;
4. observes the automatic full-reload error output.

open.body: ### Describe the bug Assets X are not correctly provided when those 3 conditions are met: 1. Vite is served with `bundledDev: true` 2. An asset A is imported with `?url` ```ts // main.js import stylesUrl from './styles.css?url' // stylesUrl results in the correct URL ``` 4. open.title: Vite does not resolve `modulepreload` for plugin-resolved IDs
open.body:
### Describe the bug

When an HTML entry contains a module preload link pointing at a source module, it gets followed when doing `vite build`:

```html
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/src/main.ts" />
<script type="module" src="/src/main.ts"></script>

<!-- ⬆️ the above is transformed to the below ⬇️ -->

<link rel="modulepreload" href="data:text/javascript;base64,..." />
<script type="module" src="/assets/index-....js"></script>
```

But if the JS module is a plugin-resolved ID, it doesn't follow the `modulepreload`:

```html
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/@plugin-script" />
<script type="module" src="/@plugin-script"></script>

<!-- ⬆️ the above is transformed to the below ⬇️ -->

<link rel="modulepreload" href="/@plugin-script" /> ❌
<script type="module" src="/assets/index-....js"></script>
```

In Dev mode it's fine because Vite will respond to `/@plugin-script`, but in Build mode the ID stays the same so it leads to a 404 (or an unrelated file). 

In the same way as with "real" files, the plugin-provided IDs should be followed.

I've run into this while building SSR on top of Vite, where adding the client entry through React's prerender API [(`prerenderToNodeStream` → `options` → `bootstrapModules`)](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/prerenderToNodeStream#prerender:~:text=optional-,bootstrapModules,-%3A%20Like%20bootstrapScripts%2C%20but), it always emits both the `<script>` tag and the corresponding `<link>` tag. But in our solution, this client entry is an virtual file we create in a plugin, so the `<script>` loads fine, but the `<link>` doesn't.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-fuhrkwp2?file=index.html

### Steps to reproduce

Run `npm install` followed by `npm run start`. It will start the Vite preview server.
Check your network devtools, there should be a 404 for a `/@plugin-script` modulepreload even though the script itself was loaded fine.

open.title: Migrating asset handling on top of Rolldown's built-in handling
open.body:
# Why?

- Vite has some codes copied from Rollup and it is harder to keep them consistent.
- It is confusing to have Vite's own system for plugin authors: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15306, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/13459, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/17559
- It makes it difficult to create a plugin that works with both Rolldown and Vite. For example, we were not able to extract the wasm plugin part as a rolldown plugin because the asset handling is not aligned.
- It is inefficient to process the code on Vite side while Rolldown can do it
- It makes it easier to support https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/20360, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19945, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/20070

# What is needed to done?

Replace `__VITE__ASSET__` with [Rolldown's `import.meta.ROLLUP_FILE_URL_referenceId `](https://rolldown.rs/apis/plugin-api/file-urls#file-urls) feature. Find out missing feature on the Rolldown side to achieve that. We may need to figure out whether the distinction of `this.emitFile({ type: 'asset' })` and `this.emitFile({ type: 'chunk' })` in Rolldown makes sense anymore as `moduleType`s feature exists.

open.title: `vite preview` HTTP/2: `@polka/compression` wrapping breaks `text/event-stream` — concurrent fetches stall on the same connection
open.body:
### Describe the bug

`vite preview` unconditionally registers `@polka/compression` ahead of every response (`packages/vite/src/node/preview.ts:239 — app.use(compression())`). When a request has `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, polka wraps `res.writeHead`/`write`/`end`/`on` and defers `writeHead` to its `start()` function — even when the response is `text/event-stream` and won't actually be compressed (chunked SSE has no `Content-Length`, fails polka's `size >= threshold` check).

Under HTTP/2 (which `vite preview` enables when `preview.https` is set), this wrapping corrupts the HTTP/2 stream lifecycle when the SSE stream is aborted client-side. Other `fetch` calls multiplexed on the same connection get stuck `pending` for 10–30 seconds before resolving, or never resolve. Page navigations away from any route that holds an open SSE stream stall visibly.

The compression itself is not the issue — it's correctly skipped for SSE due to the size threshold. The bug is in the proxying of `res` methods that happens *before* the compression decision.

### Suggested fix

Skip polka's response wrapping for `text/event-stream` in `vite preview`. Possible shapes:

- bump the bundled `@polka/compression` once [lukeed/polka#221](https://github.com/lukeed/polka/pull/221) or equivalent lands
- guard `app.use(compression())` in `packages/vite/src/node/preview.ts` to skip SSE paths
- expose a `preview.compression` option so consumers can opt out


### Reproduction

https://github.com/rsergeenko/vite-preview-sse-http2-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install && npm run build && npm run preview`
2. Open `https://localhost:4173/` (accept the self-signed cert)
3. Click **Open SSE** — opens a long-lived `text/event-stream` connection via `fetch`
4. Wait ~2 seconds (a couple of events stream)
5. Click **Fetch /data** — issues a concurrent `GET /data` (small JSON response)
6. DevTools → Network: observe `/data` sits **`pending` for 10–30 seconds** before resolving

**Expected:** `/data` resolves in single-digit ms.

### System Info

```shell
- Vite 8.0.16 (also reproduces on 7.x)
- Node 22.x
- macOS 25.5.0, Chromium 148
- @polka/compression 1.0.0-next.25 (bundled with Vite)
```

yarn

open.title: ssr.target: 'webworker' invokes esmExternalRequirePlugin() with an empty `external`, so bundled CJS require("<node builtin>") is left as a throwing __require stub
open.body:
### Describe the bug

Follow-up to #21969 / #21963 (merged, in 8.0.15). I intend to submit a PR for this if maintainers agree on the approach below.

PR #21963 made `ssr.target: 'webworker'` SSR builds use `platform: 'browser'` and added `esmExternalRequirePlugin()` so external CJS `require()` calls become ESM imports — fixing the `createRequire(import.meta.url)` startup crash on Cloudflare Workers (workerd).

However, a **CommonJS dependency that internally calls `require("<node builtin>")`** (e.g. `node-forge` doing `require("crypto")`) is still not handled, because the plugin is invoked **without an `external` option**:

```js
// resolved webworker SSR build — esmExternalRequirePlugin is added with no `external`
if (isSsrTargetWebworkerEnvironment) {
  plugins.push(esmExternalRequirePlugin())   // empty `external` ⇒ matches nothing
}
```

With an empty `external`, the plugin converts nothing, so the bundled module's nested `require("crypto")` falls through to Rolldown's `__require` runtime stub:

```js
var crypto = __require("crypto");
// __require throws: Calling `require` for "crypto" in an environment that doesn't
// expose the `require` function. (https://rolldown.rs/in-depth/bundling-cjs#require-external-modules)
```

This crashes on workerd (no global `require`). In a framework that evaluates the SSR output during build analysis (e.g. SvelteKit `adapter-cloudflare`), the **build itself fails** at this stub.

By contrast, Vite 7 / Rollup statically converts the same nested `require("crypto")` into `import nodeCrypto from "crypto"`, which works on workerd. So this is a regression for the webworker target.

**Expected:** for webworker SSR, Vite should pass the node builtins / resolved externals to the plugin, i.e. `esmExternalRequirePlugin({ external: [/^node:/, ...nodeBuiltins] })`, so nested builtin `require()` in bundled CJS is converted to ESM imports (which workerd's `nodejs_compat` then resolves).

**Demonstrated fix** (see the repro's `vite.config.fix.js`): building with `esmExternalRequirePlugin({ external: [/^node:/, 'crypto'] })` turns the stub into a real ESM import:

```js
import * as m from "crypto";
var crypto = require_builtin_esm_external_require_crypto();   // -> m.default
```



### Reproduction

https://github.com/basuke/vite-webworker-cjs-require-repro

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm run build          # vite build, uses vite.config.js (ssr.target: 'webworker')
cat dist/entry.js      # -> contains `var crypto = __require("crypto")` (throwing stub)
```

Fix demonstration:

open.title: Windows: a file imported via both a tsconfig `paths` alias and a relative path is bundled twice (non-normalized back-slash module id)
open.body:
### Describe the bug

> **AI disclosure:** 
>
> I used an AI assistant to isolate this down to the minimal reproduction and to review this description.
>
> The bug was first observed in a real codebase; the reproduction is human-reviewed and CI-verified.

On Windows, a production build duplicates a module when **one physical file is imported through both a relative specifier and a `tsconfig.json` `paths` alias**. This is NOT the "two different files" case (cf. #22351); it is a single file that resolves to two module ids differing only by slash direction:

- relative `./shared` `->` `C:/dev/.../src/shared/index.js` (forward slashes)
- alias `@shared/index` `->` `C:\dev\...\src\shared\index.js` (back slashes)

Rolldown keys its module graph on the raw id string, so it treats these as two separate modules and emits two copies. **The proof that it's the same file (and a normalization bug, not intended behavior) is the platform asymmetry: on Linux both specifiers resolve to one forward-slash id and the module is bundled once; only on Windows is it duplicated.** Any module-level singleton is therefore duplicated on Windows. In the real app where I hit this, the duplicated module held a `React.createContext`, so the Provider and a `useContext` bound to different context objects and the app threw "must be used within a Provider", at runtime, from a default build, only on Windows.

This happens with **no plugins and the default config**. The alias is resolved by Vite/Rolldown's native `tsconfig.json` `paths` handling, active at the default `resolve.tsconfigPaths: false`. I isolated it:

- Reproduces with **zero Vite plugins** and **no manual `resolve.alias`**. Renaming `tsconfig.json` so it can't be found makes the build fail with `Rolldown failed to resolve import "@shared/index"`, confirming the tsconfig-`paths` resolver is what resolves it.
- Vite's own `resolve.alias` is **not** affected; it normalizes to a single forward-slash id (no duplication).
- Setting **`resolve.tsconfigPaths: true` works around it** (resolution then routes through Vite's normalized handling `->` one forward-slash id `->` one module). So the buggy state is the default `false`.

**Where the fix likely belongs:** Vite's tsconfig-`paths` resolution should normalize the resolved id (e.g. via `normalizePath`) before returning it. Rolldown declined to normalize ids internally (rolldown/rolldown#2303, closed wontfix), so the normalization has to happen on the Vite side. This looks like another instance of the Windows path-normalization family also seen in #15153 (duplicate module from a relative `rollupOptions.input`) and #22264 (backslash-vs-POSIX mismatch breaking HMR).

**Expected:** one physical file resolves to one canonical module id whether reached via a relative path or a tsconfig `paths` alias, so it's bundled once (as it already is on Linux).
**Actual:** two ids (back-slash vs forward-slash) on Windows `->` bundled twice `->` duplicated module-level singleton.

I'm not planning to open a PR myself, but happy to test a fix.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/caillou/vite-windows-alias-duplication

### Steps to reproduce

The repro is a single file `src/main.js` that imports `src/shared/index.js` via both `./shared` and the `@shared/*` tsconfig path. `src/shared/index.js` exports `const TOKEN = Symbol('shared-singleton')`; `main.js` asserts the two imports are `===`.

On **Windows**:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run repro      # = vite build && node dist/index.js
```

- **Actual (Windows):** the build reports an extra module; `node dist/index.js` prints `DUPLICATED` and exits 1 (the two `TOKEN` imports are not `===`). `dist/index.js` contains `Symbol('shared-singleton')` twice.
- **Expected / on Linux:** prints `OK`, exits 0, single module instance.

The repo's GitHub Actions matrix runs this on `ubuntu-latest` (green, `OK`, 3 modules) and `windows-latest` (red, `DUPLICATED`, 4 modules) on every push.

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
    CPU: (16) x64 INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C
    Memory: 44.85 GB / 63.99 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.15.0 - C:\nvm4w\nodejs\node.EXE
    pnpm: 10.33.0 - C:\nvm4w\nodejs\pnpm.CMD
  Browsers:
    Edge: Chromium (148.0.3967.54)
  npmPackages:
    vite: 8.0.10 => 8.0.10
    rolldown: 1.0.0-rc.17  (transitive of vite; not listed by envinfo)
```

### Used Package Manager

pnpm

### Logs

<details>
<summary>Click to expand!</summary>

```shell
# the two ids Rolldown sees for the same file src/shared/index.js (captured with a load() hook):
"C:/dev/vite-windows-alias-duplication/src/shared/index.js"   <- relative  ./shared
"C:\dev\vite-windows-alias-duplication\src\shared\index.js"   <- alias @shared/index (tsconfig paths)

# vite build: 4 modules transformed on Windows (duplicated) vs 3 on Linux
```
</details>

open.title: Vite 8.0.14 dep-optimizer corrupts lone-surrogate Unicode escapes (\uD800-\uDBFF) in regex strings
open.body:
### Describe the bug

Starting with Vite **8.0.14** (which bumps `rolldown` 1.0.0-rc.18 → 1.0.2 and lands [#22342](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22342) "pass oxc jsx options to transformSync in dependency scan"), the dep-optimizer corrupts lone-surrogate Unicode escape sequences in CommonJS-imported string literals.

For an input regex string like:

```js
// node_modules/@vscode/markdown-it-katex/.../katex.js (CJS, transitively loads KaTeX)
var tokenRegexString = "([!-\\[\\]-‧‪-퟿豈-￿][̀-ͯ]*|[\uD800-\uDBFF][\uDC00-\uDFFF][̀-ͯ]*|..."
```

The dep-optimized output at `node_modules/.vite/deps/@vscode_markdown-it-katex.js` is:

```js
"([!-\\[\\]-‧‪-퟿豈-￿][̀-ͯ]*|[<FFFD>d800-<FFFD>dbff][<FFFD>dc00-<FFFD>dfff][̀-ͯ]*..."
```

The escapes whose decoded values are **valid BMP characters** (`‧`, `‪`, `퟿`, `豈`, `￿`) survived. But the escapes whose decoded values are **lone surrogates** (`\uD800`, `\uDBFF`, `\uDC00`, `\uDFFF`) were each turned into a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER followed by literal text `d800` etc. The resulting `[<FFFD>d800-<FFFD>dbff]` is parsed by the JS regex engine as a character class containing the literal characters `<FFFD>`, `d`, `8`, `0`, `-`, `b`, `f` — no longer matching surrogate code units in input strings.

For KaTeX's lexer (which uses this regex), the practical impact is that every multi-character control word longer than the backslash escape gets truncated — `\sqrt` tokenizes as `\s` (red error) plus the letters `qrt` as math italics, breaking all rendered math.

This appears to be a UTF-8 round-trip step in the dep-optimizer's minification path that doesn't handle lone surrogates (UTF-8 explicitly cannot represent them; the encoder substitutes U+FFFD).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/CluesOverride/td148-vite-lone-surrogate-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/CluesOverride/td148-vite-lone-surrogate-repro && cd td148-vite-lone-surrogate-repro`
2. `npm install`
3. `npx vite dev`
4. Open `node_modules/.vite/deps/@vscode_markdown-it-katex.js` and search for `dbff` — you'll see `<U+FFFD>d800-<U+FFFD>dbff` instead of `\uD800-\uDBFF`.
5. Open the browser to `http://localhost:5173/`. The page's self-check table will show `SOURCE PRESERVED? NO`, and `\sqrt{x}` renders as `\s` (red) + literal math-italic `qrtx`.
6. Re-install with `npm install vite@8.0.13 --save-exact` and re-run `npx vite dev` — the cache file contains preserved `\uD800` escapes with zero U+FFFD bytes; KaTeX renders correctly.

Bug is in DEV-mode dep-optimizer specifically — `vite build` preserves the escapes (the build path uses a different minifier code path).

### Expected behavior

The optimized bundle preserves the original string semantics. Lone-surrogate escape sequences in JS string literals should either:
- Remain as `\uXXXX` escape sequences in the output (safest), OR
- Be preserved as round-tripping JavaScript string values (each lone surrogate is one UTF-16 code unit; `"\uD800".charCodeAt(0) === 0xD800` is well-defined).

Vite 8.0.11 / 8.0.12 / 8.0.13 (rolldown 1.0.0-rc.18) preserves the strings correctly. The behavior change in 8.0.14 (rolldown 1.0.2 + #22342) appears to assume strings can be re-encoded via UTF-8 round-trip, which silently corrupts lone surrogates.

### Actual behavior

Each `\uD800-\uDBFF` and `\uDC00-\uDFFF` escape becomes `<U+FFFD>d800-<U+FFFD>dbff` etc. The JS regex engine parses the corrupted character class differently than the source intended, and downstream consumers (KaTeX's lexer) fail. Six U+FFFD bytes appear in `node_modules/.vite/deps/@vscode_markdown-it-katex.js` under 8.0.14, zero under 8.0.13.

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 26.5
    CPU: (14) arm64 Apple M4 Pro
    Memory: 396.00 MB / 48.00 GB
    Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 22.22.2 - /Users/austinfee/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.22
    npm: 10.9.7
    pnpm: 11.2.2
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 148.0.7778.179
    Firefox: 149.0
    Safari: 26.5
  npmPackages:
    vite: 8.0.14 => 8.0.14
    rolldown (transitive): 1.0.2
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

Not applicable — bug is in the optimized bundle bytes on disk, not in `vite --debug` console output.

- [x] No existing duplicate issue (searched lone-surrogate / surrogate / unicode-escape-regex / KaTeX-dep-optimizer / 8.0.14-regex / Oxc-transformSync / Rolldown-minify-string)

open.title: SSR module runner exposes incomplete `export *` facade namespace in cold circular imports
open.body:
### Describe the bug

## Description

Vite module runner can expose an incomplete facade namespace during cold SSR evaluation when a facade imports a module, later re-exports `*` from the same module, and an intervening dependency cycles back to the facade.

This can cause valid native ESM to fail in SSR with runtime errors like:

```txt
TypeError: createThing is not a function
```
## Reduced Module Graph
```txt
facade.js
  |
  | import { createStart } from './core.js'
  v
core.js
facade.js
  |
  | export { client } from './client.js'
  v
client.js
  |
  v
start.js
  |
  v
middleware.js
  |
  | import { createThing } from './facade.js'
  v
facade.js
  |
  | returns partial in-flight namespace
  v
missing createThing from later export * from './core.js'
```

## Reduced Source Shape
```js
// facade.js
import { createStart } from './core.js'
export { client } from './client.js'
export * from './core.js'
export { createStart }
```
```js
// core.js
export var createThing = (value) => value
export var createStart = () => {
  return { started: true }
}
```
```js
// client.js
import { start } from './start.js'
export const client = start()
```
```js
// start.js
import { createStart } from './facade.js'
import { middleware } from './middleware.js'
export function start() {
  return { ...createStart(), middleware }
}
```
```js
// middleware.js
import { createThing } from './facade.js'
export const middleware = createThing('middleware')
```

## Expected Behavior
This works in native ESM:
```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import('./facade.js').then((m) => console.log(m.client))"
```
Expected output:
```txt
{ started: true, middleware: 'middleware' }
```
The circular import observes `createThing` through the facade because `facade.js` already imported `./core.js` before evaluating the client re-export.
## Actual Behavior
In Vite SSR/module-runner, the circular import can observe the facade before the later transformed `export * from './core.js'` has registered its runtime `__vite_ssr_exportAll__()` getters.
The facade namespace is returned as partial exports, but it does not contain the wildcard export yet.
Result:
```txt
TypeError: createThing is not a function
```
## Real-World Case
This appears in TanStack Start cold SSR startup (see https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/7459).
The public `@tanstack/react-start` facade imports `@tanstack/react-start-client`, and that client path eventually imports `#tanstack-start-entry`, which points back to the app's `src/start.ts`.
At the same time, app code imports `createStart` / `createMiddleware` from `@tanstack/react-start`.
Simplified graph:
```txt
src/start.ts
  |
  | import { createStart } from '@tanstack/react-start'
  v
@tanstack/react-start
  |
  | import { Hydrate } from '@tanstack/react-start-client'
  v
@tanstack/react-start-client
  |
  | export { hydrateStart }
  v
@tanstack/start-client-core/client/hydrateStart
  |
  | import { startInstance } from '#tanstack-start-entry'
  v
src/start.ts
  |
  | imports middleware
  v
middleware.ts
  |
  | import { createMiddleware } from '@tanstack/react-start'
  v
@tanstack/react-start
  |
  | partial in-flight facade namespace
  v
missing createMiddleware from export * from '@tanstack/start-client-core'
```
The package facade has this emitted shape:
```js
import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/start-client-core'
import { Hydrate } from '@tanstack/react-start-client'
export * from '@tanstack/start-client-core'
export { Hydrate, createServerFn, useServerFn }
```
Since `createMiddleware` is only available through `export *`, Vite's partial namespace does not include it when the cycle returns.

### Reproduction

see above

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### System Info

```shell
reproduced with vite 8.0.14
```

pnpm

_No response_

open.title: Support separate CSP nonces for scripts and styles
open.body:
### Description

Vite currently supports `html.cspNonce` as a single shared nonce placeholder.

This works for many setups, but some CSP integrations generate separate nonces for `script-src` and `style-src`. A concrete example is `@fastify/helmet`: with `enableCSPNonces: true`, it exposes:

```js
reply.cspNonce.script
reply.cspNonce.style
```

and adds them to `script-src` and `style-src` respectively.

With the current Vite API, users either need to collapse both values into one nonce or add custom handling around Vite-generated tags.

### Suggested solution

Allow `html.cspNonce` to accept either the current string value or a split object:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  html: {
    cspNonce: {
      script: '__SCRIPT_NONCE__',
      style: '__STYLE_NONCE__',
    },
  },
})
```

Expected behavior:

- `string` keeps the current shared nonce behavior;
- `script` nonce is used for scripts and script preloads;
- `style` nonce is used for styles and style preloads;
- existing `meta[property="csp-nonce"]` integrations keep working as fallback.

### Alternative

A partial workaround is to avoid using Vite's single nonce for scripts and rely on `script-src 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic'` for script loading, while using the existing Vite nonce meta tag only for style-related runtime injections:

```html
<meta property="csp-nonce" nonce="STYLE_CSP_NONCE" />
```

This can make style preloads work because Vite reads `meta[property="csp-nonce"]` when injecting runtime preload/style links.

However, this is a split and implicit setup.

### Additional context

I have an open PR with a possible implementation in Vite core: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22289

It keeps the existing shared `html.cspNonce` behavior and adds an opt-in `{ script, style }` mode for split CSP nonce setups.

open.title: Failed automatic server restarts don't release the port immediately

open.title: postcss-import content-hash dedup silently drops Tailwind v4 `@source` from byte-identical files
open.body:
### Describe the bug

Vite's bundled `postcss-import` deduplicates `@import`-ed CSS files by **content hash** (when the imported file contains no nested `@import`). Two CSS files at different paths but with byte-identical content are treated as duplicates and the second is silently skipped.

This breaks Tailwind v4's `@source` directive when it's used in a per-package `sources.css` pattern — a common workspace setup where each package has a `src/styles/sources.css` containing just:

```css
@source "../**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}";
```

If two packages happen to have byte-identical `sources.css` files, the second package's `@source` is never processed. Tailwind never scans that package, no utilities are generated, components silently render unstyled. The error is **silent**: no warning, no broken import, no missing-file error.

The `@source` directive is *path-dependent* (the relative pattern resolves against the file's own location), so dedup-by-content is wrong for it: the two imports have identical bytes but represent **different scan targets**.

### Reproduction

Minimal repro: https://github.com/notxcain/vite-postcss-source-dedup-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/notxcain/vite-postcss-source-dedup-repro
cd vite-postcss-source-dedup-repro
npm install
npm run build
grep -F '.text-\[42px\]'   dist/assets/index-*.css   # → 1 match  (pkg-a)
grep -F '.leading-\[1\.7\]' dist/assets/index-*.css  # → 0 matches (pkg-b dropped)
```

`src/styles.css` uses `@import "tailwindcss" source(none);` to disable Tailwind's automatic content detection — utilities can only enter the build via the explicit `@source` directives in the two packages' `sources.css` files. Both files have byte-identical content (`@source "./*.html";`); only the first one's `@source` runs.

Swap the import order to flip which class gets compiled. Make a single byte differ between the two `sources.css` files (e.g. add `/* pkg-b */` at the top of one) and **both** classes appear.

### Root cause

In `node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/postcss-import.js` (Vite's bundled fork of `postcss-import`):

```js
// skip previous imported files not containing @import rules
if (
  options.skipDuplicates &&
  state.hashFiles[content]?.[stmtDuplicateCheckKey]
) {
  return
}
…
if (options.skipDuplicates) {
  const hasImport = styles.some(child =>
    child.type === "atrule" && child.name === "import"
  );
  if (!hasImport) {
    if (!state.hashFiles[content]) state.hashFiles[content] = {};
    state.hashFiles[content][stmtDuplicateCheckKey] = true;
  }
}
```

`skipDuplicates: true` is the default. Files without nested `@import` are cached by content; subsequent imports with identical content short-circuit. Reasonable for CSS resets, wrong for files whose at-rules carry path-relative side effects.

### Expected behavior

A path-dependent at-rule like Tailwind v4's `@source` (or `@plugin`, `@config`) should not be dropped by content-hash dedup, since two byte-identical files at different locations express different intent.

### Suggested fix

Skip content-hash dedup when the file contains any path-dependent at-rule. Narrowest fix matches the same set Tailwind's own `tailwindcss-postcss-fix-relative-paths` plugin already walks (`@source`, `@plugin`, `@config`):

```js
const hasPathDependentAtRule = styles.some(child =>
  child.type === "atrule" &&
  (child.name === "import" ||
   child.name === "source"  ||
   child.name === "plugin"  ||
   child.name === "config")
);
if (!hasPathDependentAtRule) {
  // …existing content-dedup caching…
}
```

A broader fix could disable content-dedup whenever any unknown at-rule is present, on the principle that `postcss-import` shouldn't assume the semantics of at-rules it doesn't own.

### System Info

```
Vite: 8.0.10
@tailwindcss/postcss: 4.2.4
tailwindcss: 4.2.4
Node: v22 (also reproduced on bun 1.3.1)
OS: macOS 14 (Darwin 24.6.0)
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

open.title: Disconnect HMR WebSocket on pagehide for BFCache compatibility
open.body:
### Description

[BFCache](https://web.dev/articles/bfcache) is a browser performance feature that enables instant back/forward navigation. It would be useful to have BFCache work in Vite dev environments so that navigation performance can be tested and developed against accurately. Currently this is not possible: browsers [disqualify pages with open WebSocket connections](https://web.dev/articles/bfcache#never-use-unload-event) from BFCache, and Vite's `@vite/client` keeps an HMR WebSocket open for the lifetime of the page.

### Suggested solution

In `packages/vite/src/client/client.ts`, add [`pagehide`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/pagehide_event)/[`pageshow`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/pageshow_event) listeners alongside the existing `beforeunload` block:

```ts
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.addEventListener?.('pagehide', () => {
    transport.disconnect?.()
  })
  window.addEventListener?.('pageshow', async (event: PageTransitionEvent) => {
    if (event.persisted) {
      await transport.connect!(createHMRHandler(handleMessage))
    }
  })
}
```

[`unload`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/unload_event) and [`beforeunload`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeunload_event) are intentionally avoided as registering listeners for either also disqualifies pages from BFCache.

### Alternative

- Export `transport` from `client.ts` so downstream integrations can manage the lifecycle themselves. This adds API surface and places the burden on each integrator rather than fixing it universally.
- Downstream integrations could wrap `window.WebSocket` before `@vite/client` loads to intercept and hold a reference to the socket. This relies on script ordering and internal implementation details.

open.title: [bug] 504 Outdated Optimize Dep on lazy-route navigation — dep optimizer bumps per-subpath ?v= after transform is served
open.body:
### Describe the bug

When a lazy-loaded module (dynamic `import()`) reaches a dependency subpath that Vite's dep optimizer hasn't seen yet, the optimizer re-runs mid-navigation and bumps the per-subpath `?v=` hash. Any already-served module whose transformed output hard-codes the **previous** `?v=` for that subpath now points at a URL Vite rejects with `504 Outdated Optimize Dep`. The dynamic `import()` then fails with:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../Counter.lazy.tsx
```

The root cause is not in the lazy module — it's in a **transitive** optimized-dep chunk whose hash is now stale relative to the module that imports it.

This is distinct from #17738 (missing chunk file on disk), #20609 (metadata/in-memory hash divergence across restarts), and #13506 (404-served-as-504). They're in the same failure family, but none describes **lazy mid-navigation subpath discovery causing hash bumps** as the trigger.

### Concrete trigger in the repro

- `@tanstack/start-plugin-core` calls `crawlFrameworkPkgs` and adds any workspace package that declares `@tanstack/react-start` in its `peerDependencies` to `optimizeDeps.exclude`. The esbuild scanner does not follow imports into excluded workspaces.
- In the repro, the Button subpath is only reachable through `modules/demo/src/counter/Counter.lazy.tsx` (which is in an excluded workspace), so `react-aria-components/Button` is NOT pre-bundled at cold start. `react-aria-components/Link` and `.../composeRenderProps` ARE pre-bundled because they're reached via the eagerly-imported RootLayout.
- On first `/counter` navigation, Vite transforms the lazy chunk's wrapper, discovers `react-aria-components/Button`, optimizes it, assigns hash `A`, embeds `?v=A` in the served wrapper — then promotes it into a fresh optimization batch with hash `B`. The browser's subsequent fetch for `?v=A` returns 504.

### Network trace (representative)

Different `?v=` hashes across different optimized deps indicate the optimizer ran several passes during one navigation:

```
react.js                        ?v=3d6ef4f8
react-aria-components_Link.js   ?v=e2b427fe
react-aria-components_Button.js ?v=c2f17a43    ← 504 Outdated Optimize Dep
@tanstack/* chunks              ?v=81e69589
```

### Expected behavior

Either:

1. Vite invalidates / re-transforms modules whose downstream optimized-dep hashes changed during a lazy discovery pass (so the served wrapper always references the current hash), OR
2. Vite serves the current chunk regardless of `?v=` when only the hash has changed and the underlying content is equivalent.

Today the workaround is to manually enumerate every subpath in `optimizeDeps.include`. For libraries like `react-aria-components` that publish ~40 per-component subpaths, this is error-prone: forgetting any subpath only imported from a rarely-visited lazy route (especially one in a workspace that's excluded via `crawlFrameworkPkgs`) leaves a latent 504.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/patricklafrance/vite-rac-tsr-504-repro

26 files, verified **5 / 5** 504s on a fresh clone using the included headless-Chrome CDP script.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/patricklafrance/vite-rac-tsr-504-repro
cd vite-rac-tsr-504-repro
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open http://localhost:5173 and click the **Counter** link. DevTools Network will show a `504 Outdated Optimize Dep` on `react-aria-components_Button.js?v=<hash>`, and the console will log `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`.

To verify programmatically, run the bundled CDP harness against a headless Chrome — see README "Automated reproduction" section. 5/5 runs produce the 504.

### Workaround

Uncommenting this block in `apps/web/vite.config.ts` fixes the issue:

```ts
optimizeDeps: {
    include: ["react-aria-components/Button"]
}
```

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
  CPU: (24) x64 AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370
  Memory: 22.78 GB / 55.65 GB
Binaries:
  Node: 24.13.0
  pnpm: 10.30.1
Browsers:
  Chrome: 147.0.7727.102
npmPackages:
  vite: 8.0.9
  @vitejs/plugin-react: 6.0.1
  @tanstack/react-start: 1.167.42
  @tanstack/react-router: 1.168.23
  @netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start: 1.3.7
  @tailwindcss/vite: 4.2.4
  react-aria-components: 1.17.0
  react, react-dom: 19.2.5
```

### Used package manager

pnpm

### Related

- #17738 — missing `.vite/deps/chunk*` (disk-level staleness, different trigger)
- #20609 — metadata/in-memory hash divergence across restarts (fixed)
- #13506 — 504-vs-404 semantics (cosmetic)
- #14284 — 504 after `--force` race (restart-triggered)
- discussion #14801 — "optimized dependencies changed and reloading many times" (closest, focused on the reload storm rather than the 504 failure surface)

open.title: CSS bundle order is incorrect
open.body:
### Describe the bug

My main entry point starts with
```js
import "virtual:uno.css"
import "./Components/Css/index.css";
// Then JS imports, some of which have associated CSS because of <style> tag in Vue SFC.
```

But when bundling for production, the `index.css` chunk, containing unocss output and the `index.css` imported above, comes last.
This can be observed with `cssCodeSplit: true` because that `index.css` is last included in html, or with `cssCodeSplit: false` because its content is last in the merged css bundle.

I have debugged the issue when `cssCodeSplit: false` and will explain below what happens.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-1tvfcfrw?file=src%2Fmain.js

### Steps to reproduce

Idea in repro above is that main.js imports style.css first, then indirectly counter.js imports counter-style.css next.
Counter-style overrides the .counter color to red, which is what happens in dev mode, live in vite.new.
I don't know how to test a production bundle on vite.new, but I expect the order of scripts to be reversed (and the counter to be black).
I explain why below.

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Windows 11 10.0.26100
    CPU: (20) x64 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1370P
    Memory: 11.85 GB / 31.64 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 25.9.0 - C:\Users\***\scoop\apps\nodejs\current\node.EXE
    npm: 11.12.1 - C:\Users\***\scoop\apps\nodejs\current\npm.CMD
  Browsers:
    Edge: Chromium (143.0.3650.75)
    Internet Explorer: 11.0.26100.7309

Not sure why that command doesn't list Vite version, anyway:
Vite: 8.0.9
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

I have debugged the issue, when `cssCodeSplit: false`.
The culprit is the `collect` function here, which attempts to preserve order:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts#L1010-L1022

It tries to include in order: the static imports, then the dynamic imports, then the module own styles.

The key issue is that when a JS module does `import "style.css"`, this isn't listed in `chunk.imports`.
Instead, the CSS ends up attached to current chunk in `chunkCSSMap`, which is added last.

In my own project, moving the line 
`extractedCss += chunkCSSMap.get(chunk.preliminaryFileName) ?? ''`
first solves the issue, but I don't think it's the right fix, for two reasons:
1. It doesn't solve the ordering issue amongst static import. What if `import "virtual:uno.css"` wasn't the first import in my file and we had JS with an indirect CSS import first?
2. It's probably incorrect for chunks representing Vue components with `<style>` tags, those ones should come after static imports.

I believe the right fix is for Vite to create one empty chunk for each `import "xyz.css"`, that is listed in `chunk.imports` in correct order, and attach the `chunkCSSMap` to this chunk instead.
Everything should then be in right order.

open.title: SSR transform's hoisted export getter silently returns undefined for re-exports in cycles (spec says ReferenceError)
open.body:
### Describe the bug

I am using Vite's SSR module loader (both `server.ssrLoadModule` and the Vite 8 environment API `server.environments.ssr.runner.import`) to evaluate modules that use `export * as X from './…'` in an import cycle.

**What I expect** — per ES module spec, and as demonstrated by native `import()` under both Node and Bun — is that accessing the re-exported namespace during the cycle window throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'X' before initialization`. The namespace object itself is stable; reading a member whose inner binding is in TDZ throws loudly.

**What actually happens** — Vite's SSR transform wraps every exported binding in `try { return ${local} } catch {}` (the `defineExport` helper in `packages/vite/src/node/ssr/ssrTransform.ts`, hoisted above the `await __vite_ssr_import__(...)` lines). When the cycle peer reads the re-export before its `const` is initialized, the `catch {}` silently swallows the TDZ `ReferenceError` and returns `undefined` — for the entire namespace binding.

Consumer code like `const Root = Namespace.Root` at module top-level then crashes downstream with a confusing `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating '…')` far from the real cause.

The `try/catch` is self-flagged as provisional in PR #19959 (merged 2025-05-02, commit `fd38d07`, first shipped in 6.3.5):

> We'll revisit whether we should remove `try/catch` after investigating that further.

This issue is the follow-up — with a deterministic repro and a confirmation that it is **not** specific to the runtime (both node and bun), not specific to the vite version (reproduces on 7.3.2 stable and 8.0.0), and not specific to the legacy API (reproduces on the new environment API too).

Not submitting a PR — leaving the design call to maintainers (options in the "Steps" notes below).

> Drafted and researched by Claude Opus 4.7; reviewed and filed by me. 

### Reproduction

Minimal repro (4 JS files + driver, ~30 lines of user code total). I can push to a public repo and paste the URL here if needed. Full source included in Steps.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Create a project:
   ```bash
   mkdir ssr-cycle-repro && cd ssr-cycle-repro
   bun init -y
   bun add -d vite@8.0.0
   ```
2. Create `modules/sub.js`:
   ```js
   export const a = 1;
   ```
3. Create `modules/cyc-a.js`:
   ```js
   import { valueFromB } from './cyc-b.js';
   export * as Ns from './sub.js';
   export const valueFromA = 'A:' + valueFromB;
   ```
4. Create `modules/cyc-b.js`:
   ```js
   import { Ns as NsFromA } from './cyc-a.js';
   export const valueFromB = 'B-value';
   export const NsKeys = NsFromA ? Object.keys(NsFromA) : 'NsFromA_IS_UNDEFINED';
   export const maybeA = NsFromA ? NsFromA.a : 'NsFromA_WAS_UNDEFINED';
   ```
5. Create `test-cycle.js`:
   ```js
   import { createServer } from 'vite';
   import path from 'node:path';
   import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

   const server = await createServer({
       root: path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),
       configFile: false,
       logLevel: 'silent',
       server: { middlewareMode: true },
       appType: 'custom',
       optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: true }  // only for determinism; not load-bearing
   });

   await server.ssrLoadModule('/modules/cyc-a.js');
   const b = await server.ssrLoadModule('/modules/cyc-b.js');
   console.log('NsKeys =', b.NsKeys);
   console.log('maybeA =', b.maybeA);
   await server.close();
   ```
6. Run: `node test-cycle.js`

**Expected output** (if behavior matched native ESM): a `ReferenceError` during cycle resolution.

**Actual output:**
```
NsKeys = NsFromA_IS_UNDEFINED
maybeA = NsFromA_WAS_UNDEFINED
```

**Native-ESM comparison** — same three `modules/*.js` files, no Vite:
```bash
$ node -e "import('./modules/cyc-a.js').then(async () => { const b = await import('./modules/cyc-b.js'); console.log(b.NsKeys, b.maybeA); })"
```
```
file:///.../modules/cyc-b.js:7
export const NsKeys = NsFromA ? Object.keys(NsFromA) : 'NsFromA_IS_UNDEFINED';
                                       ^
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'a' before initialization
    at Object.keys (<anonymous>)
    at file:///.../modules/cyc-b.js:7:40
```

Spec-correct TDZ throw. Vite's SSR loader swallows it.

### Coverage matrix (reproduced identically)

| Runtime | Vite version | API | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node 25.6.1 | 8.0.0 | `server.ssrLoadModule` | silent `undefined` |
| Bun 1.3.13 | 8.0.0 | `server.ssrLoadModule` | silent `undefined` |
| Node 25.6.1 | 8.0.0 | `server.environments.ssr.runner.import` | silent `undefined` |
| Bun 1.3.13 | 8.0.0 | `server.environments.ssr.runner.import` | silent `undefined` |
| Node 25.6.1 | **7.3.2 stable** | `server.ssrLoadModule` | silent `undefined` |
| Bun 1.3.13 | **7.3.2 stable** | `server.ssrLoadModule` | silent `undefined` |

Not rolldown-vite-specific. Not runtime-specific. `defineExport` helper unchanged on `main` as of 2026-04-21.

### Production build (`vite build --ssr`) — also silently-undefines, different mechanism

For completeness: running the same three files through `vite build --ssr` and executing the built artifact under node or bun prints the same fallback strings:
```
NsKeys = NsFromA_IS_UNDEFINED
maybeA = NsFromA_WAS_UNDEFINED
```
The built output shows `var`-hoisting ordering the dependency read before the dependency is defined:
```js
//#region modules/cyc-b.js
var valueFromB = "B-value";
var NsKeys = sub_exports ? Object.keys(sub_exports) : "NsFromA_IS_UNDEFINED";  // sub_exports is `undefined` here
var maybeA = sub_exports ? 1 : "NsFromA_WAS_UNDEFINED";
//#endregion
//#region modules/sub.js
var sub_exports = /* @__PURE__ */ __exportAll({ a: () => 1, b: () => 2, greet: () => greet });
```

This is a different mechanism (rolldown `var` hoisting vs. SSR transform getter with try/catch) but the same spec-divergent outcome. I'm filing this issue specifically about the SSR transform because that's the one with the self-flagged `try/catch` TODO — but flagging the build-side behavio
