open.title: HMR silently skipped on Windows when file is imported via npm workspace symlink (backslash path from watcher doesn't match POSIX `moduleGraph.fileToModulesMap` keys)
open.body:
### Describe the bug On Windows, when a source file is imported through an npm workspace symlink (e.g. `node_modules/@scope/pkg` → `/packages/pkg`), the dev server watcher correctly receives `change` events for the realpath, but Vite silently skips HMR for those modules. Root cause: - `server.watcher` emits `change` with a Windows-native path using backslashes, e.g. `C:\repo\packages\pkg\src\index.ts`. - `server.moduleGraph.fileToModulesMap` is keyed by POSIX paths with forward slashes, e.g. `C:/repo/packages/pkg/src/index.ts`. - `getModulesByFile(rawBackslashPath)` returns `undefined`, `getModulesByFile(normalizedSlashPath)` returns the expected module set. - Because the lookup fails, Vite has no module to invalidate and never sends an HMR / full-reload message to the client. Saving the file appears to do nothing in the browser. Files inside the Vite project root (no symlink indirection) are unaffected because Vite's own path handling produces consistent POSIX keys throughout. This same root cause was acknowledged in [nuxt/nuxt#19179](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/19179) (merged Jan 2023): *"path coming from the watcher contains backslash on Windows, while Vite's `getModulesByFile` does not handle that... potential bug of Vite."* Nuxt patched it downstream; as far as I can find, no upstream Vite issue has the specific `watcher-path separator / moduleGraph key` asymmetry documented. Related but not duplicate: #16176, #6479, #10558 all discuss Windows + symlink HMR issues but pin the blame on `preserveSymlinks`, which is the wrong axis — the symlink resolution itself works fine, it's the path-separator normalization between `watcher.change` and `moduleGraph` that breaks HMR. ### Reproduction http://localhost:5173 ### Steps to reproduce Minimal repro on Windows (PowerShell or Git Bash): ``` mkdir vite-hmr-win-repro && cd vite-hmr-win-repro npm init -y npm pkg set "workspaces[0]=packages/*" mkdir -p packages/lib/src app ``` `packages/lib/package.json`: ```json { "name": "@test/lib", "type": "module", "exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" } } ``` `packages/lib/src/index.ts`: ```ts export const msg = "hello v1"; ``` `app/index.html`: ```html
``` `app/main.ts`: ```ts import { msg } from "@test/lib"; document.getElementById("out")!.textContent = msg; ``` `vite.config.ts` (in repo root): ```ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; export default defineConfig({ root: "app" }); ``` ``` npm i -D vite typescript npm i npx vite ``` Open `http://localhost:5173`, confirm "hello v1" is displayed. Edit `packages/lib/src/index.ts`, change the string to `"hello v2"`, save. **Expected:** Browser updates to "hello v2" (HMR or full reload). **Actual:** No network activity, browser still shows "hello v1". Vite terminal shows no HMR message despite the watcher firing internally. Diagnostic plugin that confirms the mismatch: ```ts { name: "diag", configureServer(server) { server.watcher.on("change", (p) => { const norm = p.replace(/\\/g, "/"); console.log( "change:", p, "| raw=", server.moduleGraph.getModulesByFile(p)?.size, "| slash=", server.moduleGraph.getModulesByFile(norm)?.size, ); }); }, } ``` Output on file save (Windows): ``` change: C:\...\packages\lib\src\index.ts | raw= undefined | slash= 1 ``` ## Workaround A 15-line plugin that normalizes watcher paths, invalidates the module via the POSIX key, and triggers full-reload manually: ```ts function winPathNormalizePlugin() { return { name: "win-path-normalize", configureServer(server) { server.watcher.on("change", (filePath) => { if (!filePath.includes("\\")) return; const normalized = filePath.replace(/\\/g, "/"); const mods = server.moduleGraph.getModulesByFile(normalized); if (!mods || mods.size === 0) return; for (const mod of mods) server.moduleGraph.invalidateModule(mod); server.ws.send({ type: "full-reload", path: "*" }); }); }, }; } ``` The proper upstream fix is to normalize the path inside Vite's watcher-change handler before it hits `getModulesByFile`, analogous to what Nuxt does in its wrapper. ### System Info ```shell - **Vite**: 7.3.1 - **Node**: 22.19.0 - **OS**: Windows 11 (26200) - **Shell tested in**: Git Bash, PowerShell (both reproduce) - **Package manager**: npm (workspaces) ``` ### Used Package Manager npm ### Logs (Vite output with the diagnostic plugin above) ``` change: C:\repo\packages\lib\src\index.ts | raw= undefined | slash= 1 ``` No `hmr update` or `page reload` line ever appears without the workaround. ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vite.dev/guide). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. For example, if it's a Vue SFC related bug, it should likely be reported to [vuejs/core](https://github.com/vuejs/core) instead. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions) or join our [Discord Chat Server](https://chat.vite.dev/). - [x] The provided reproduction is a [minimal reproducible example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) of the bug.

open.title: ?raw import of large file with many newlines causes OOM (153x memory amplification from sourcemap generation)
open.body:
### Describe the bug

Importing a large text file via `?raw` causes the Vite dev server to crash with a V8 OOM (`FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`, exit code 134).

The `?raw` handler in the `vite:asset` plugin has no file size check and reads the entire file unconditionally:

```js
// src/node/plugins/asset.ts - load hook
if (rawRE.test(id)) {
  const file = checkPublicFile(id, config) || cleanUrl(id);
  this.addWatchFile(file);
  return `export default ${JSON.stringify(await fsp.readFile(file, "utf-8"))}`;
}
```

This creates multiple in-memory copies (raw file + JSON.stringify result + template literal). The critical amplification comes after this hook returns: Vite's `send()` function generates a fallback source map via:

```js
new MagicString(code).generateMap({
  source: path.basename(urlWithoutTimestamp),
  hires: "boundary",      // character-level mappings
  includeContent: true    // embeds full code in sourcesContent
})
```

For a file with millions of lines, the `hires: "boundary"` source map is enormous. The result is cached persistently in `moduleGraph`, so GC cannot reclaim it.

The newline ratio is the critical factor because it affects both JSON.stringify expansion (1 byte `\n` → 2 bytes `\\n`) and the number of source map boundary entries.

### Measured impact (Vite 8.0.3, Node 24.10.0, 2048MB heap limit)

**Response size multiplier (input → dev server response):**
- 0% newlines: **2.3x** (e.g. 100MB file → 233MB response)
- 10% newlines: **3.8x** (e.g. 100MB file → 385MB response)
- 50% newlines: **10.3x** (e.g. 20MB file → 207MB response)

**OOM thresholds with 2048MB heap (`NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=2048"`):**

| File Size | 0% newlines | 10% newlines | 50% newlines |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|--------------|
| 20MB      | ok          | ok           | ok           |
| 25MB      | —           | —            | **OOM**      |
| 50MB      | ok          | ok           | **OOM**      |
| 100MB     | ok          | ok           | **OOM**      |
| 110MB     | —           | **OOM**      | —            |
| 150MB     | ok          | **OOM**      | **OOM**      |
| 200MB     | ok          | **OOM**      | **OOM**      |
| 300MB     | ok          | —            | —            |

**Approximate failure thresholds (2048MB heap):**
- 0% newlines: >300MB
- 10% newlines: ~100–110MB
- 50% newlines: ~20–25MB

With the default Node heap (~1.5GB on this 14GB system), the thresholds would be lower. A 231MB file with ~50% newlines (the real-world case that triggered this investigation) OOMs reliably.

**Workaround:** Use `?url` + `fetch` instead:

```js
const filterUrls = import.meta.glob('./data/*.txt', { query: '?url' });
const mod = await filterUrls[path]();
const response = await fetch(mod.default);
const text = await response.text();
```

This is related to #11745 (closed, fixed in Vite 4.5) which addressed the same root cause (magic-string sourcemap OOM) but the fix reduced the multiplier from ~100x to ~5-7x, which is still fatal for moderately large files with many lines.

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz link (too large for online repro). Minimal reproduction via shell:

```bash
npm create vite@latest repro -- --template vanilla && cd repro && npm install
mkdir data
# Generate 20MB file with 10M lines (50% newlines)
python3 -c "import sys; [sys.stdout.write('x\n') for _ in range(10_000_000)]" > data/test.txt
```

Add to `src/main.js`:
```js
const loaders = import.meta.glob('../data/*.txt', { query: '?raw' });
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=2048" npx vite`
3. `curl http://localhost:5173/data/test.txt?import&raw`
4. Observe: server crashes with exit code 134, `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 7.0 Ubuntu 25.10 25.10 (Questing Quokka)
    CPU: (12) arm64 unknown
    Memory: 8.40 GB / 14.44 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.2.37 - /bin/bash
Binaries:
    Node: 24.10.0
    npm: 11.6.1
    pnpm: 10.25.0
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

- [x] Follow our Code of Conduct

- [x] Read the docs

- [x] Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue

open.title: Suggestion: backend-only mode
open.body:
### Description

I recently started working on a new project. It's a backend-only project, using express.

Almost by reflex, I tried using Vite for it, when I realised that's not what Vite is for. But why wouldn't it? It has a lot of features I love and need:
- plugins - import glob, directly import various resources (e.g. yaml configuration files), etc.
- dev server - I don't _need_ a front-end, but I'd love to be able to run my app, change something, and it instantly restarts; no build needed
- testing - amazing test runner and just works with my plugins/build pipeline
- build - self-explanatory
- environment variables & modes
- serving static files



### Suggested solution

I'd love a simple, official Vite plugin for backend-only apps. It creates a single environment (no client vs. ssr), with `dev` and `build` commands that work with the standard plugins & Vitest.

I feel like this makes sense now more than ever with Vite Plus, which offers so much more than `dev` and `build`. Vite was created as a tool for web developers, but with how popular and feature-rich it is now, and with the new environments API meant to support more than just client + SSR mode, this feature really feels like a missing puzzle piece.

### Alternative

I ended up using rolldown directly, with rolldown & node watch mode for the dev server, and making the pipeline work with Vitest, which was quite a bit of work, and is not perfect.

There also are third-party plugins like [vite-express](https://github.com/szymmis/vite-express), but I think an official, generic solution would be all-around very useful.

In short, there is a bit of friction, which a minimalist Vite plugin could easily get around. I don't see why Vite(+) with such a plugin wouldn't be used for non-web work, even if just as a light wrapper over rolldown to simplify the setup & improve the experience.


### Additional context

If this sounds like a good idea, I'm happy to work on & try contributing this feature 🙂

open.title: Module runner caches by bare specifier URL, serves wrong version for duplicate dependencies
open.body:
### Description

The module runner's `urlToIdModuleMap` caches modules keyed by their URL. When a bare specifier (e.g., `@azure/core-lro`) is used as the URL — which happens when the import analysis plugin treats it as external and doesn't resolve it — the first resolved version is cached and served to all subsequent importers, even if they should receive a different physical package.

Additionally, the `{ cache: true }` protocol between the module runner (client) and the Vite server has no identity verification. When the client sends `{ cached: true }` for a module, the server checks if the *server-side resolved* module was already transformed and returns `{ cache: true }` if so. But the server's resolution may point to a different physical package than what the client has cached. The client interprets `{ cache: true }` as "use what you have" and serves the stale/wrong version.

### Location

`packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts`:

**Cache lookup** — `urlToIdModuleMap` maps URLs to modules. For bare specifiers used as URLs, this collapses multiple physical packages into one entry:
```js
getModuleByUrl(url) {
  return this.urlToIdModuleMap.get(url);  // "foo" → first resolved version
}
```

**`{ cache: true }` protocol** — `cachedModule` / `getModuleInformation`:
```js
// Client side: "I have this module cached"
fetchResult = await this.transport.fetchModule(url, { cached: true });
// Server side: resolves url → different physical path, sees it was transformed → { cache: true }
// Client side: uses stale cached module ← WRONG
```

### Impact

Given two versions of a package in a monorepo:
1. First import: `@azure/core-lro` resolved to v2.7.2, externalized, loaded into runner → cached as `urlToIdModuleMap["@azure/core-lro"] = v2.7.2 module`
2. Fourth import: `@azure/core-lro` resolved to v3.x by server, transformed, stored under `/@fs/.../core-lro@3.x/...` URL
3. Fifth import: `getModuleByUrl("@azure/core-lro")` → returns v2.7.2 (stale cache hit). Client sends `{ cached: true }`. Server resolves to v3.x, sees it was transformed → `{ cache: true }`. Client serves v2.7.2 → crash:

```
SyntaxError: The requested module '@azure/core-lro' does not provide an export named 'deserializeState'
```

### Suggested fix

1. **Cache key**: `urlToIdModuleMap` should not accept bare specifiers as keys, or should resolve them to full paths before caching.
2. **`{ cache: true }` protocol**: Include the resolved file path or a content hash so the client can verify it has the correct module, not just *a* module with the same URL.

### Relation to other issues

This was discovered alongside a `processedIds` cache bug (#22078) and a vitest `configEnvironment` bug ([vitest#10028](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10028)). All three are independent correctness issues that compound when multiple versions of a dependency exist in a pnpm workspace.

### System Info

```
vite/7.3.1
pnpm/10.33.0
node/v22.22.1
```

open.title: SSR externalization cache (processedIds) ignores importer, serves wrong decision for duplicate dependencies
open.body:
### Description

`createIsExternal` in Vite's SSR externalization logic caches decisions in a `processedIds` Map keyed solely by the bare specifier string, ignoring the importer. When two importers should resolve the same bare specifier to different physical packages (valid in pnpm/npm with nested `node_modules`), the first resolution's externalization decision is served to all subsequent importers.

### Location

`packages/vite/src/node/ssr/ssrExternal.ts` — the `processedIds` map in `createIsExternal`:

```js
const processedIds = new Map<string, boolean | undefined>();

async function isExternal(id: string, importer?: string) {
  if (processedIds.has(id)) {
    return processedIds.get(id);  // ← importer ignored
  }
  // ... resolves using importer, caches result by id only
  processedIds.set(id, result);
}
```

### Impact

Given this dependency tree (common in monorepos):
- Package A → `foo@2.x` (in `node_modules/.pnpm/foo@2.0.0/`)
- Package B → `foo@3.x` (in `node_modules/.pnpm/foo@3.0.0/`)

If Package A's import is processed first:
1. `isExternal("foo", "package-a/index.js")` → resolves to `foo@2.x` → `canExternalizeFile` → `true` → cached as `processedIds["foo"] = true`
2. `isExternal("foo", "package-b/index.js")` → `processedIds.has("foo")` → returns `true` (cached) → **wrong**: Package B's `foo@3.x` might not be externalizable (or should resolve differently)

The cache key should incorporate the importer (or the resolved path) to distinguish different physical packages behind the same bare specifier.

### Reproduction context

This was discovered via [vitest#10028](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10028), where the cache causes `@azure/core-lro@2.7.2`'s externalization result to be applied to `@azure/core-lro@3.x`, leading to unresolved bare specifiers reaching the module runner.

### Suggested fix

Use the resolved path (or a composite key of specifier + resolved path) as the cache key instead of the bare specifier alone.

### System Info

```
vite/7.3.1
pnpm/10.33.0
node/v22.22.1
```

### Describe the bug

After upgrading to Vite@8, I noticed that CSS minification now defaults to Lightning CSS. Since then, production builds started showing warnings or failing when using some modern progressive CSS features that are already supported in browsers.

Examples include selectors and pseudo-elements such as
`::scroll-marker`, `::scroll-marker-group`, `::scroll-button()`, `:target-current`, and `::search-text`.

@scope (.section) {
  color: blue;
}

Switching the CSS minifier back to `esbuild` resolves the issue.

This feels more like a tooling constraint than a platform limitation. Vite has traditionally provided a very standards-friendly developer experience, so it would be great if progressive modern CSS usage remained smooth by default.

npm run build

open.title: CSS cascade order differs between dev and production when using auto-imported component styles
open.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `vite-plugin-vuetify` with `autoImport: true`, the CSS cascade order between dev mode and production builds is inconsistent in Vite 8. This causes visual regressions where styles render differently in production.

**In dev mode**, CSS `<style>` tags are injected in module-load order:
1. Statically imported CSS (e.g. `import 'material-design-icons-iconfont/dist/material-design-icons.css'`)
2. Auto-imported component CSS (e.g. VIcon CSS, loaded lazily when the component first renders)

Since the component CSS loads **after** the static import, component rules like `.v-icon--size-default { font-size: calc(var(--v-icon-size-multiplier) * 1.5em) }` win over `.material-icons { font-size: 24px }` (same specificity, later source order wins).

**In production**, Rolldown places the auto-imported component CSS **before** the statically imported CSS in the output bundle. This reverses the cascade: `.material-icons { font-size: 24px }` now comes after `.v-icon--size-default` and wins, causing icons to render at a fixed 24px instead of the relative `1.5em` size, and `display: inline-block` instead of `display: inline-flex`.

The result is icons that appear **bigger and bolder** in production builds compared to dev mode.

### Reproduction

Entry point imports a Vuetify plugin:

```js
// src/plugins/vuetify.js
import { createVuetify } from 'vuetify'
import 'vuetify/styles'
import { aliases, md } from 'vuetify/iconsets/md'
import 'material-design-icons-iconfont/dist/material-design-icons.css'

export default createVuetify({
  icons: { defaultSet: 'md', aliases, sets: { md } },
})
```

With `vite-plugin-vuetify` configured with `autoImport: true`:

```js
// vite.config.mjs
vuetify({ autoImport: { labs: true, directives: true } })
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Vuetify 3 app using `vite-plugin-vuetify` with auto-import and `material-design-icons-iconfont`
2. Add any `<v-icon>` to a page
3. Run `npm run dev` — icons render at the correct relative size (`1.5em`)
4. Run `npm run build && npx vite preview` — icons render at a fixed `24px`, appearing larger

### Evidence from build output

In the production CSS output, VIcon's CSS chunk appears early while the material-icons CSS ends up much later in the main index chunk:

```
VIcon CSS:            byte offset ~5,587   → .v-icon--size-default { font-size: calc(...1.5em) }
material-icons CSS:   byte offset ~340,440 → .material-icons { font-size: 24px }
```

Both selectors have the same specificity (single class), so the later one wins — which is `.material-icons` in production but `.v-icon--size-default` in dev mode.

### Expected behavior

The CSS cascade order in production builds should match dev mode. Statically imported CSS should appear **before** auto-imported component CSS in the production output, preserving the same cascade resolution.

### Actual behavior

Production builds reverse the order: auto-imported component CSS appears before statically imported CSS, changing which rules win the cascade for same-specificity selectors.

### Workaround

Wrapping the icon font CSS import in a CSS `@layer` ensures consistent cascade priority regardless of source order:

```css
/* src/assets/css/material-icons.css */
@import 'material-design-icons-iconfont/dist/material-design-icons.css' layer(icon-fonts);
```

Unlayered styles (Vuetify component CSS) always take precedence over layered styles, making the result order-independent.

### Relation to #21826

This appears to be the same underlying issue reported in #21826, which was closed for lack of a minimal reproduction. The root cause is that Rolldown (introduced in Vite 8 via `beta.15`) reorders CSS extraction, changing the cascade for same-specificity selectors between dev and production.

open.title: Expose command (build/serve) and environment name in import.meta.env
open.body:
### Description

Frameworks built on Vite, and sometimes user code itself, need a way to detect if it's running through `vite serve` or after `vite build`. It looks like the ecosystem itself is a bit confused about how to detect it. E.g. Vike seems to be using `NODE_ENV`, earlier versions of Rakkas were using `import.meta.env.MODE`, neither of which is appropriate since `NODE_ENV` is for _runtime_ environment and `import.meta.env.MODE` can be set to `"development"` or `"production"` independently from the Vite command, e.g. with the `--mode` CLI argument.

A related but separate issue is how to get the current environment name. `import.meta.env.SSR` was good enough when there were only two environments but the new API requires a new way to get the current environment name.

### Suggested solution

I propose a new `import.meta.env.COMMAND` entry that will resolve to `"serve"` or `"build"` depending on the command Vite is running with.

A related but separate nice-to-have would be a way to access the current environment name. I think an explicit `import.meta.env.ENVIRONMENT` that would be replaced with `"client"`, `"ssr"` , `"rsc"` etc. would be nice to have both for framework authors and, sometimes, user code.

### Alternative

Admittedly, these are not hard to implement in a plugin. But I feel they are such fundamental problems needed to be solved by every framework or app that they belong to the core.

closed.title: server.forwardConsole: forwarded objects are serialized without a depth/size limit (one console.warn can emit ~1 MB)
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

When `server.forwardConsole` is enabled, object arguments in forwarded console calls are fully serialized on the client and printed to the dev server terminal without any depth or size limits.

A single `console.warn` containing a large (finite, non-circular) object tree (6^6 = 46,656 leaf nodes) prints a single line of 951,852 characters (~0.95 MB) to the terminal (measured with Vite 8.3.0).

For comparison, logging the same object natively remains lightweight: browser devtools store a live reference with a collapsed preview, and Node's console (`util.inspect`, default depth of 2) outputs only ~5 KB for the same tree.

Impact:

- Vue's dev-mode warnings pass component instances to `console.warn` as part of the component trace. A component instance pulls in the entire reactivity graph, serializing to ~1.5 MB per warning (circular references are already handled via `[Circular]` markers — the issue is the sheer breadth). A warning fired on every render adds megabytes of terminal output per page load.
- `forwardConsole` is enabled by default when an AI coding agent is detected. Because agents typically capture dev server output, a single recurring warning can flood the agent's context window.

Expected behavior: Summarize object arguments with a depth/size cap (similar to devtools previews or Node's `util.inspect` defaults), or truncate the formatted output at a maximum length.

https://github.com/ryuhei373/vite-forwardconsole-repro

2. Open the page and click the "console.warn a large object (once)" button

closed.title: [v8] tsconfig auto-discovery eagerly loads the whole project-references graph and hard-fails when any referenced project extends an uninstalled config package
closed.body:
### Expected

Per the docs, `resolve.tsconfigPaths` makes `paths` apply "to a file matched by a `tsconfig.json` through its `files` or `include`". In a monorepo where the root tsconfig is a solution-style file with `references` (a layout TypeScript recommends for project references), a referenced project whose tsconfig `extends` a config package — a devDependency of *that* project only — should not affect an unrelated build, especially under a partial install (`pnpm install --filter <pkg>` / filtered installs) where that package is intentionally absent.

### Actual

Any file not covered by a nearby tsconfig's `include` (e.g. a config/helper file imported from source, outside every `include` scope) triggers the upward tsconfig auto-discovery up to the workspace root tsconfig. Loading it eagerly traverses **all** `references` and resolves **every** `extends` — including projects entirely unrelated to the current build. If any of those `extends` targets is not installed, **all** module resolution and transform in the Vite instance fails:

```
Error: Tsconfig not found @nonexistent/config-pkg/base
```

This is **not** limited to `resolve.tsconfigPaths: true`: with the option set to `false`, the `vite:oxc` transform path performs its own tsconfig auto-discovery and fails the same way:

```
[TSCONFIG_ERROR] Failed to load tsconfig '@nonexistent/config-pkg/base': Tsconfig not found
❯ transformWithOxc node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js
```

### Reproduction (self-contained — no attachment needed)

Everything below is reproducible from an empty directory. Tested with **Node v24.20.0** and **npm 11.19.0**; the only dependency versions that matter are pinned in `package.json` (`vite@8.2.2` ships `rolldown@~1.2.4`, resolving to **rolldown 1.2.7**, which locks `oxc_resolver 11.24.3`; `vitest` is pinned to the exact verified version **4.1.11**).

Create this tree (9 files):

```
repro/
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json                  # workspace root: solution-style (files: [] + references)
├── vitest.config.ts
├── workspace-app/
│   ├── tsconfig.json              # clean: has paths + include:["src"]
│   ├── config/
│   │   └── code.ts                # OUTSIDE include -> triggers upward discovery
│   └── src/
│       ├── index.ts
│       └── entry.test.ts
└── other-app/
    ├── tsconfig.json              # extends a config package that is NEVER installed
    └── src/
        └── x.ts
```

File contents:

**`package.json`**

```json
{
  "name": "vite8-tsconfig-not-found-repro",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "vite": "8.2.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "vitest": "4.1.11"
  }
}
```

**`tsconfig.json`**

```json
{
  "files": [],
  "references": [
    { "path": "./workspace-app" },
    { "path": "./other-app" }
  ]
}
```

**`vitest.config.ts`**

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({
  resolve: { tsconfigPaths: true },
  test: { include: ['workspace-app/src/**/*.test.ts'] },
});
```

**`workspace-app/tsconfig.json`**

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "paths": { "@app/*": ["src/*"] }, "baseUrl": "." },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

**`workspace-app/src/index.ts`**

```ts
export const a = 1;
```

**`workspace-app/src/entry.test.ts`**

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { a } from './index';
import { cfg } from '../config/code';
test('repro', () => { expect(a).toBe(1); expect(cfg).toBeDefined(); });
```

**`workspace-app/config/code.ts`** — the key trigger: it lives **outside** `include: ["src"]`, so discovering its owning tsconfig walks up to the root; it imports a bare specifier, so the resolver consults tsconfig paths while resolving it.

```ts
import { expect } from 'vitest';
export const cfg: string = typeof expect;
```

**`other-app/tsconfig.json`** — the missing config package `@nonexistent/config-pkg` is **deliberately never installed**; nothing in the test's import graph uses `other-app`; it is only reachable through the root tsconfig's `references`.

```json
{
  "extends": "@nonexistent/config-pkg/base",
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

**`other-app/src/x.ts`**

```ts
export const c = 3;
```

Run:

```
npm install
npx vitest run
```

**Expected**: the single test passes — `other-app`'s tsconfig is irrelevant to `workspace-app`'s test, and per the docs `paths` only applies to files matched through `files`/`include`.

**Actual** (exit code 1):

```
Error: Tsconfig not found @nonexistent/config-pkg/base
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  no tests
```

### Controls (each changes exactly one thing)

| # | Change | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `vitest.config.ts`: set `resolve.tsconfigPaths: false` | **Still fails** — `[TSCONFIG_ERROR] Failed to load tsconfig '@nonexistent/config-pkg/base': Tsconfig not found` in `transformWithOxc` (the `vite:oxc` transform path auto-discovers independently of the option) |
| 2 | `tsconfig.json`: replace `references` with none (keep `{"files": []}`) | **Passes** — no references graph to traverse |
| 3 | `other-app/tsconfig.json`: remove the `extends` line | **Passes** — graph is fully resolvable |
| 4 | `tsconfig.json`: move the `references` array into a sibling `tsconfig.node.json` (root `tsconfig.json` keeps only `{"files":[]}`); run vitest from the sub-project directory with the vitest config there | **Passes** — auto-discovery only opens files named exactly `tsconfig.json`; a differently-named sibling (the solution-file pattern from the TS docs) is never read |

### Root cause (source-mapped against rolldown v1.2.7 tag and oxc-resolver v11.24.3 tag)

- `crates/rolldown_plugin_vite_resolve/src/resolver.rs:187-193`: `tsconfigPaths: true` without an explicit config file maps to `TsconfigDiscovery::Auto`.
- oxc-resolver v11.24.3 `find_tsconfig_auto`: walks parent directories per resolved file; **each candidate tsconfig is fully loaded (its `extends` chain and its whole `references` graph) before** checking whether it owns the file via `claims_ownership_of`.
- `load_tsconfig` / `get_extended_

closed.title: isInNodeModules check is too loose
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

If the path to your project contains the substring "node_modules", many vite features break. The simplest one to demonstrate is that inline script tags in HTML break.

My reproduction below is the stock vite vanilla blueprint with a single inline script tag added to index.html. All that's needed to reproduce the bug is to name the project "node_modules_bug".

In the specific case of the inline script tag, the failure happens because [ensureVersionQuery](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/29a260cb16025408defc2e8186d1fbf17ee099ac/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L522) incorrectly decides that `index.html?html-proxy&index=0.js` is in node_modules and rewrites it to `index.html?v=af416d6b&html-proxy&index=0.js`, which then fails to match the [regex in html-inline-proxy](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/29a260cb16025408defc2e8186d1fbf17ee099ac/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/html.ts#L49), because that regex only works when `html-proxy` is the first search param in the URL.

At a minimum, `isInNodeModules` should probably require path separators on both sides of the `node_modules` string. This would fix my specific reproduction, but would still leave people broken who happen to have a project root with an ancestor directory named "node_modules" (which is definitely a thing sometimes when dealing with legacy codebases).

A complete fix would make `isInNodeModules` aware of the configured [root](https://vitejs.dev/config/shared-options.html#root), because whether or not a given path comes into your project via node_modules is ultimately a question relative to that root:

```
Given: 

  root=/path/to/node_modules/your-project

Then:

  inNodeModules("/path/to/node_modules/your-project/x", root) -> false because x is clearly in our configured root
  inNodeModules("/path/to/node_modules/your-project/node_modules/y", root) -> true because we left the configured root "inward"
  inNodeModules("/path/to/node_modules/z", root) -> true because we left the configured root "outward"
```

### Reproduction

https://github.com/ef4/node_modules_bug

1. Clone the above repo (using the default directory naming, which will put the project in a directory named "node_modules_bug").
2. pnpm install

closed.title: `experimental.bundledDev`: `hotUpdate` runs without environment injection (`this.environment` undefined), leaving stale output until restart
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

Under `experimental.bundledDev`, a plugin's `hotUpdate` hook is invoked with `this.environment` undefined. Reading `this.environment` is the documented way to scope `hotUpdate` behavior (https://vite.dev/changes/hotupdate-hook), so plugins following the docs throw a `TypeError` on every file edit.

Mechanism, as far as we can tell from the source (checked on `main` and `v8.1.5`):

- `ROLLUP_HOOKS` (`packages/vite/src/node/constants.ts`) includes `watchChange` but not `hotUpdate`.
- `injectEnvironmentToHooks` (`packages/vite/src/node/build.ts`) wraps `resolveId`/`load`/`transform` explicitly and every other hook only `if (ROLLUP_HOOKS.includes(hook))` — so no environment-bound wrapper exists for `hotUpdate`, and under bundled dev the hook executes with the engine's bare plugin context.

The consequence is worse than a crash: the throw is captured as a build error, the dev server keeps running, and it serves **stale output on every subsequent edit until restart**. (#23024 improved terminal printing for failed HMR updates, but the hook-contract violation and the stale serving remain.) For anyone running Vite behind a wrapper — hosted dev servers, CI preview environments — this presents as "HMR silently stopped working."

Real-world occurrence: `@tanstack/start-plugin-core` reads `this.environment.name` on the first line of its `hotUpdate` hook ([plugin.ts](https://github.com/TanStack/router/blob/main/packages/start-plugin-core/src/vite/start-compiler-plugin/plugin.ts#L398-L399)) — deterministic breakage on `@tanstack/start-plugin-core` 1.171.17–1.171.34, tracked in TanStack/router#8062 (guard PR TanStack/router#8061). These versions are pulled transitively by current `@tanstack/react-start` releases, so the blast radius is every TanStack Start app trying bundled dev.

Related issues, which we believe are distinct facets of the same underlying gap:

- #23125 — the `hotUpdate` *options* object missing `server`/`timestamp`/`read` (this issue is about the `this` context instead).
- #23124 (closed, Phase 2 milestone).

closed.title: mergeConfig crashes with TypeError when server.ws is false and server.hmr is merged
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

`mergeConfig` throws an uncaught `TypeError` when merging a `server.hmr` object while `server.ws` is set to `false`:

```
TypeError: Property description must be an object: undefined
```

This also happens during normal config resolution whenever a plugin's `config`/`configResolved` hook (or a second `loadConfigFromFile` result) returns an `hmr` object on top of a base config that has `server.ws: false`.

**Root cause:** in `mergeConfigRecursively`, when the recursion reaches `server`, `setupHmrWsOptionCompat` is called. When `serverConfig.ws === false`, that helper returns early **without** defining the `wsOptionKeys` accessors on the `hmr` object. Later, when recursion reaches `server.hmr` (base and override both have an `hmr` object), `mergeConfigRecursively` unconditionally does:

```js
Object.defineProperty(
  merged,
  key,
  Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(defaults, key)!,
)
```

`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(defaults, key)` returns `undefined` because the accessors were never installed, and the non-null assertion turns into `Object.defineProperty(merged, key, undefined)` → `TypeError`.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR.

### Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/scs0209/67329ba3aa7e6ff9e12a359e696e0336

`repro.mjs`:
```js
import { mergeConfig } from 'vite'

const base = { server: { ws: false, hmr: { host: 'localhost' } } }
const override = { server: { hmr: { port: 5173 } } }

// throws:
// TypeError: Property description must be an object: undefined
console.log(mergeConfig(base, override))
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install` a project with `vite` (>= 6, reproduced on `v8.3.0` and `main`)
2. Run the snippet above, or start a dev server where a plugin's `config` hook returns:
   ```js
   config() {
     return { server: { ws: false } }
   }
   ```
   while another plugin's `config` hook returns `{ server: { hmr: { host: '...' } } }`
3. Observe the `TypeError` instead of a merged config

<details>
<summary>System Info</summary>

- Vite: reproduced on `v8.3.0` and current `main`
- Node.js: v26.0.0
- npm: 11.12.1
- OS: macOS (arm64)
</details>

closed.title: Every in-process server.restart() keeps the previous environments alive (rolldown builtin-plugin callbacks held as global handles)
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

Each in-process `server.restart()` keeps the previous server's environments alive. The trigger is any `vite.config.*` or `.env` change. On a real TanStack Start app, five restarts took the dev server from 1.4 GB to 5.3 GB. Heap after GC grew by about 370 MB per restart.

The minimal reproduction below uses no plugins. After 10 restarts, all 10 previous `client` environments are still reachable after GC.

Heap snapshots show the retainer. It is the JS callbacks that `oxcResolvePlugin` passes to rolldown's native `viteResolvePlugin` (`onWarn`, `finalizeBareSpecifier`, `finalizeOtherSpecifiers`, `resolveSubpathImports`). `makeBuiltinPluginCallable` wraps the plugin in a `BindingCallableBuiltinPlugin`, and the native side holds those functions as global handles (napi references). Each callback closes over `getEnv` / `partialEnv`, so the old environment graph is reachable from a GC root:

```
(GC roots) → (Global handles) → closure onWarn
  → context.getEnv → context.envs → .client DevEnvironment → .moduleGraph EnvironmentModuleGraph
```

The same chain shows up through `resolveSubpathImports` and `finalizeOtherSpecifiers`. The cycle runs JS plugin → native object → global handle → closure → environment → plugin container → JS plugin, and V8 cannot collect a cycle that goes through a strong native reference. The code is unchanged in vite 8.3.0 / rolldown 1.2.10.

Possible directions, untested: release the callable builtin plugin's references when its environment closes, or have the callbacks read the environment through a holder that `close()` clears.

### Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/light-merlin-dark/9020b8ec75cf88da42550a91b62f0008

### Steps to reproduce

```
npm install
npm run repro   # node --expose-gc repro.mjs 10
```

Output:

```
{"vite":"8.3.0","node":"v22.22.3","restarts":10,"previousClientEnvironmentsStillAlive":10,"heapUsedMB":17}
```

With `0` restarts the count is `0`. The result is the same on Node v24.21.0. The heap delta is small here because the graph is one module; with a real app it is the whole transformed module graph per restart.

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: macOS 26.6.2
  CPU: (16) arm64 Apple M4 Max
  Memory: 48.00 GB
Binaries:
  Node: 22.22.3 (also reproduced on 24.21.0)
  npm: 12.0.2
npmPackages:
  vite: 8.3.0 => 8.3.0
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

N/A (memory retention, no error output).

closed.title: `server.close()` hangs forever when a dependency is discovered mid-optimize (optimizer never settles its `processing` promise)
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

**What I'm doing:** running a Vitest browser-mode suite (`vitest run`, which drives a Vite dev server) on a cold optimizer cache, where dependencies are discovered progressively while the dep optimizer is still running.

**What I expect:** once the tests finish, `vitest run` exits.

**What actually happens:** the tests pass, but `vitest run` never exits — the process hangs indefinitely and has to be killed manually. The hang is the Vite dev server's `close()` never resolving during teardown.

**Root cause** — `createDepsOptimizer()` (`packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/optimizer.ts`) leaves a `depOptimizationProcessing` promise permanently unresolved when the server is closed while an optimize run is in flight:

- The optimizer tracks pending work with a *current* `depOptimizationProcessing` promise plus a queue of enqueued ones. A dep discovered via `registerMissingImport` gets `optimizedDepInfo.processing` set to the *current* promise; `startNextDiscoveredBatch()` later moves it into the queue.
- On shutdown these are settled inconsistently: `runOptimizer()`'s **pre-optimize** `closed` guard resolves the current **and** the enqueued promises; its **post-optimize** `closed` guard resolves **only** the enqueued ones; and `close()` resolves **neither**.
- So a dep discovered into the *current* batch while a run is in flight keeps a forever-pending `.processing`. Its `vite:optimized-deps` `load()` awaits `info.processing` forever → the request never leaves `environment._pendingRequests` → `DevEnvironment.close()`'s drain loop (`while (this._pendingRequests.size > 0) await ...`) never finishes → `close()` never resolves.

Reproduced on **vite 8.0.8** and **8.1.4**.

**I intend to submit a PR.** The proposed fix is to have [`close()`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/a477454442eff649b430f9e3c6caf2500fcb7183/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/optimizer.ts#L148-L155) settle the pending promises, mirroring [`runOptimizer`'s pre-optimize `closed` guard](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/a477454442eff649b430f9e3c6caf2500fcb7183/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/optimizer.ts#L338-L343):

```diff
 async function close() {
   closed = true
+  depOptimizationProcessing.resolve()
+  resolveEnqueuedProcessingPromises()
   await Promise.allSettled([
     discover?.cancel(),
     depsOptimizer.scanProcessing,
     optimizationResult?.cancel(),
   ])
 }
```

### Reproduction

https://github.com/bent0b0x/vite-optimizer-orphan-hang

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

The test passes, then the process hangs and never exits (kill with Ctrl-C). Applying the included `fix.patch` to vite makes `npm test` exit cleanly.

The two small plugins in `vitest.config.ts` only make the race deterministic — `slow-optimize` keeps an optimize run in flight at teardown, and `slow-chain` opens a >100ms gap between dependency discoveries so one lands on the in-flight run's *current* batch. They are timing controls, not the cause: with `fix.patch` applied, the identical config exits cleanly. The same race arises naturally on a cold optimizer cache when dependencies are discovered progressively during a slow pre-bundle (e.g. a Vitest browser run with `coverage.include` + default `server.preTransformRequests`).


### System Info

```shell
System:    macOS 26.5.1, arm64 (Apple M1 Max)
Binaries:  Node 22.14.0, npm 10.9.2, pnpm 10.33.0
Browsers:  Chrome 150.0.7871.102
npmPackages:
  vite: ^8 => 8.1.4
  vitest: ^4 => 4.1.10
  @vitest/browser-playwright: ^4 => 4.1.10
  playwright: ^1.59 => 1.61.1
```

npm

closed.title: create-vite: suggestions on how to replace CJS dependencies
closed.body:
### Description

Hello my vite friends! Recently, I created my own scaffolder inspired by `create-vite`, and while developing it I found a few things that could improve `create-vite` as well. Primarily, I'm talking about the dependencies `@clack/prompts`, `mri`, and `cross-spawn`. Each one of them either is a CJS package or brings a CJS package along - and since I am ***the biggest hater of CJS***, I cannot stand this. Thankfully, most of these problems can be solved in just a few lines!!!

P.S. Turns out `@vercel/detect-agent` is also a CJS package... Sadly, I don't have a solution for this one (*who ships CJS in 2026?!*).

### Suggested solution

- `@clack/prompts`

`@clack/prompts` has a transitive dependency called `sisteransi`, which released v2.0.0 several months ago and ported the codebase to ESM with no API changes. Sadly, `@clack/prompts` still relies on the older version (1.0.5), which is still CJS. I've already opened an [issue](https://github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/issues/609) on their side asking to bump `sisteransi` to v2, but for now we can simply override the version in **pnpm-workspace.yaml**:

```yaml
overrides:
  sisteransi: "2.0.0"
```
This change is also useful because unused code from `sisteransi` can now be tree-shaken away.

- `mri`
This one is the most hilarious! By default, when the target is set to `node`, tsdown first searches for the `main:` entry in package.json and only then the `module:` entry. `mri` ships two versions:
  - CJS version for the `main:` entry
  - ESM version for the `module:` entry

If we add this to tsdown.config.ts:
```ts
{
  inputOptions: {
        resolve: {
             mainFields: ["module", "main"],
         },
  },
}
```
we flip the order so tsdown picks the correct (ESM) version of `mri`.

- `cross-spawn`
This one is harder.
`cross-spawn` is a very popular package, yet it hasn't received a single commit in the past 2 years - not great. I couldn't find any drop-in replacements... so I decided to **build one myself**! [cross-spawn-esm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cross-spawn-esm) is a modern ESM + TypeScript port with several advantages over the original: it's **~50% smaller**, has **zero dependencies**, ships types out of the box, and, of course, it's tree-shakable. The migration is very simple - check my [Migration guide](https://github.com/Timbic/cross-spawn-esm#migration-guide) for more details.

In essence:

**Before**:

```ts
import spawn from 'cross-spawn'

// line 402
const { status, error } = spawn.sync(command, args, options)
// line 624
const { status } = spawn.sync(command, replacedArgs, {
  stdio: 'inherit',
})
```

**After**:

```ts
import { spawnSync } from 'cross-spawn-esm'

// line 402
const { status, error } = spawnSync(command, args, options)
// line 624
const { status } = spawnSync(command, replacedArgs, {
  stdio: 'inherit',
})
```

I guess this is the riskiest option since the package is very new and doesn't have many downloads, but you can take a look and decide whether you want to give it a shot. After all, since you're bundling your dependencies, there's no risk even if it turns out I'm a villain about to publish a virus in the next version lmao :)

- Results:

After these changes, what do we get?
  - Fewer transitive dependencies to worry about
  - 4 kB reduction in the bundle
  - Almost a fully ESM package (*I should talk to the folks at Vercel about @vercel/detect-agent...*)
  - Since I'm the maintainer of cross-spawn-esm, you can always reach out to me if you hit any bugs or vulnerabilities - I'll patch them
 
It's not a lot, but it's honest work. If you decide against the `@clack/prompts` and `cross-spawn` changes, at least do the `mri` one so I can sleep well. After all, God's kingdom will arrive when no CJS is left in the wild ❤️

P.S. If needed, I can also open the PRs for these changes. Peace 🕊️

### Alternative

closed.title: False "points to a source file outside its package" warning for sourcemaps with a URL sourceRoot
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

When a dependency ships a sourcemap whose `sourceRoot` is a URL, the Vite dev server (SSR transform) warns once per module that the source file lies outside the package.

`injectSourcesContent` calls `computeSourceRoute`, which does `realpath(path.resolve(dirname(file), map.sourceRoot))`. For a URL that always fails, so the root is treated as missing and the map's relative `sources` are resolved with `path.resolve(sourcePath)` — i.e. against `process.cwd()` — landing outside `node_modules/<pkg>` and tripping the package-boundary check.

Packages like `domutils@3` and `entities@4` publish `"sourceRoot": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<sha>/src/"` on purpose, so devtools can fetch the original sources from the tag they were built from. `webpack://` roots hit the same code path. New majors of those packages fixed it by shipping `src/` instead (fb55/domutils#2196, fb55/entities#2084), but the old majors are still installed transitively across the ecosystem (e.g. through `htmlparser2@10` / `linkedom`).

Related: #9501 (`vite serve` vs build source resolution), though this is specifically the URL `sourceRoot` case.

I intend to submit a PR for this.

closed.title: We decided to release the [Environment API branch](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471) as `vite@6.0.0-alpha.x` (we'll continue regularly releasing new alpha patches).
closed.body:
We decided to release the [Environment API branch](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471) as `vite@6.0.0-alpha.x` (we'll continue regularly releasing new alpha patches).

The changes started by the [Runtime API](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15774) are now prompting a complete review of the way Vite handles environments (client, SSR, workerd, etc). We were originally going to release this branch as `vite@5.3.0-alpha.0` but the changes are now too big for a minor so we're going to start working on the next major directly with it. We're probably going to have ~2 months of alpha period and once we feel confident with the stability of the new APIs, we'll kick the beta.

If you are building a framework or are working in a Runtime (like the Cloudflare team), the next months are going to be very important to get the APIs right and serve as the base for the next iteration. We're thinking on lifting Vite's responsibilities to be able to share more in the ecosystem. For example, we're introducing the concept of a `ViteBuilder` that lets frameworks orchestrate all the environment builds they need to get a single `vite build` command to build the whole app. This means changing our stance on the "framework-as-a-plugin" pattern (SvelteKit, Remix, QwikCity, etc), and making it a first class pattern from Vite 6 forward.

Check out the current [Environment API docs](https://deploy-preview-16471--vite-docs-main.netlify.app/guide/api-vite-environment.html) and give us feedback. This discussion is a good place to gather it, please share your impressions and PoCs as you test.

If you think someone you know would be interested in helping us testing and creating prototypes (Workerd framework-agnostic integrations, RSC, etc), please contact them so they can get involved.

Resources:

- [Environment API PR](github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471)
- [Environment API Docs](https://deploy-preview-16471--vite-docs-main.netlify.app/guide/api-vite-environment.html)

Previous discussions:

- [Runtime API PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/12165)
- [Runtime API Feedback discussion](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15774)
- [Initial Docs PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16089)
- [Initial Implementation PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16129)

History:

Check out @antfu's [Dev SSR on Nuxt post](https://antfu.me/posts/dev-ssr-on-nuxt), explaining @pi0's [Dev Bundler idea](https://github.com/nuxt/vite/pull/201) that led to the creation of [vite-node](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/tree/main/packages/vite-node#readme). Anthony used vite-node to as the engine of [Vitest](https://vitest.dev). After revamping it, @sheremet-va added a revised version of [vite-node in Vite Core](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/12165) in Vite 5.1. The Environment API is a new iteration, deeply integrating the features vite-node provided in Vite's API.

_Originally posted by @patak-cat in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/16358_

closed.title: fix: dep-scan misses imports whose local name starts with "type"
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

`importsRE` in `packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/scan.ts` uses `(?!\s+type)` to skip TypeScript `import type` statements. Because there is no word boundary after `type`, any value import whose binding starts with the letters `type` is treated as a type-only import and skipped by `extractImportPaths`.

This is already noted as a false negative in `scan.spec.ts` (commented-out cases for `import typescript from 'typescript'`).

Affected examples:

```ts
import typescript from 'typescript'
import typeorm from 'typeorm'
import types from 'types'
```

These can be dropped from the TS/`<script setup>` crawl assist path, so esbuild may not discover those deps during optimize-deps scanning.

### Reproduction

Unit-level:

```js
const importsRE = /(?<!\/\/.*)(?<=^|;|\*\/)\s*import(?!\s+type)(?:[\w*{}\n\r\t, ]+from)?\s*("[^"]+"|'[^']+')\s*(?=$|;|\/\/|\/\*)/gm
importsRE.exec(`import typescript from 'typescript'`) // null (bug)
```

With `(?!\s+type\b)` the same import matches correctly while real `import type` forms still do not.

### System Info

Vite `main` (current).

### Used Package Manager

pnpm

### Logs

N/A (unit-reproducible)

closed.title: build.rolldownOptions.preserveEntrySignatures shows incorrect default
closed.body:
### Documentation is

- [ ] Missing
- [ ] Outdated
- [x] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

`build.rolldownOptions.preserveEntrySignatures` is documented by the underlying Rolldown type with a default value of `'exports-only'`.

However, Vite overrides this value internally depending on the build mode. For a regular client build, Vite sets it to `false`:

```ts
preserveEntrySignatures: ssr
  ? 'allow-extension'
  : libOptions
    ? 'strict'
    : false
```

This means that leaving `build.rolldownOptions.preserveEntrySignatures` undefined in a regular Vite build does not behave as the documented Rolldown default (`'exports-only'`), but as `false`.

This was confusing in my case because I have multiple TypeScript entry points whose exports are consumed as ES modules from a Blazor application. I expected the documented default to preserve those exports, but I need to explicitly set:

```ts
build: {
  rolldownOptions: {
    preserveEntrySignatures: 'exports-only',
  },
}
```

I understand that `build.rolldownOptions` is merged with Vite's internal Rolldown options, but it isn't clear that Vite overrides this particular default.

Relevant code:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/5bce8ca0f19bfdd5206c98bfabc1f8453deb32c7/packages/vite/src/node/build.ts#L658-L662

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Document the effective Vite defaults for `preserveEntrySignatures`, or otherwise mention that Vite overrides Rolldown's default.

For example:

* regular client build: `false`
* library build: `'strict'`
* SSR/server build: `'allow-extension'`

It may also be worth considering the IntelliSense/JSDoc experience, since the exposed `RolldownOptions` type reports Rolldown's `'exports-only'` default even though that is not the effective Vite default.

closed.title: Dev-server watcher silently dies when the project lives under a hardcoded-ignored path segment (e.g. **/test-results/**); defaults cannot be removed or overridden
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

Vite 8.2.2's dev-server watcher hardcodes Playwright-convention ignore patterns — including `**/test-results/**` — in `resolveChokidarOptions`, **prepended ahead of every user entry**. A project whose directory happens to live under a path segment matching those globs gets a **silently dead dev watcher**: chokidar watches zero project directories, file edits fire no events, the module graph never invalidates, HMR never emits — and a full page reload keeps serving the pre-edit modules. No warning is printed, and no `server.watch.ignored` entry can re-include the files, because anymatch ignores a path when ANY pattern matches and the defaults cannot be removed or overridden.

We hit this when a measurement harness staged project copies inside a gitignored `test-results/` directory (a natural choice — that is exactly what the glob exists to ignore tooling output for). `watcher.getWatched()` returned 0 directories over such a project; staging the identical project one directory higher made the watcher see 14+ directories and everything worked (verified on both a vite middleware-mode server and a full `vite dev` server; kernel-level `fs.watch` events were delivered in the broken case, so the files system watched — vite's chokidar filtered them out).

### Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/wojtekpiskorz/58e6ba83ab34b0d24c2d4ad04c73aeb2

1. `npm create vite@latest repro -- --template vanilla`, then `cd repro && npm i`
2. `mkdir -p ../test-results && mv ./* ../test-results/ && cd ../test-results` (any ancestor path segment named `test-results` — `**/test-results/**` — triggers it; same for the other hardcoded conventions)
3. `npx vite` and edit `src/main.js` — no HMR update arrives; with `--debug hmr` no watch events are logged; touching any file never logs `hmr update`.
4. `watcher.getWatched()` (e.g. via a tiny plugin holding `server.watcher`) prints no project directories.

### Expected

Either (a) the defaults should be removable/overridable (e.g. an explicit `server.watch.ignored: null`/reset, or documented negation that actually works given anymatch's ANY-match semantics), or (b) vite should warn when the project root itself falls under a hardcoded ignored glob — a silently dead watcher under a legitimate path is very hard to diagnose.

### Why silent-ignore is dangerous

The ignore list exists for *tooling output inside a project* (Playwright artifacts under the project root). Applied to *ancestor* path segments it ignores the entire project, and because HMR simply never fires there is no error surface at all — the failure mode looks like a caching bug in downstream tooling (we initially suspected our own proxy and module-cache discipline; bisecting staging paths found the real cause).

Verified against installed vite 8.2.2 bytes (`vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js`, `resolveChokidarOptions`), on macOS (FSEvents) and Linux (inotify).

### Basic info

- Vite version: 8.2.2 (also inspected the same hardcoded list in current main)
- Node version: 24.x
- OS: macOS 15 (arm64), Ubuntu 24.04
closed.author: wojtekpiskorz

closed.title: Feature Request: Native support for Cloudflare Workers module format in Vite build output
closed.body:
## Feature Request

### Summary

Add a dedicated **Cloudflare Workers build target** to Vite that outputs ES modules compatible with the Workers runtime without requiring manual post-processing via Wrangler.

### Motivation

Building full-stack apps with Vite + Cloudflare Workers currently requires a fragile pipeline:

1. Vite builds the server bundle
2. Wrangler re-bundles it for the Workers runtime
3. Two separate build configs must be kept in sync

This causes several pain points:

- **`process.env` shim conflicts** — Vite injects Node.js-style env shims that Workers' V8 isolate rejects
- **Dynamic `import()` is not supported** in Workers, but Vite's code-splitting can emit it
- **`__dirname` / `__filename` stubs** get injected even when targeting edge
- **Wasm imports** (`import wasmModule from './module.wasm'`) work in Workers but Vite doesn't handle them in the standard way

### Proposed Solution

Add a `target: 'cloudflare-workers'` (or `target: 'cloudflare-module-worker'`) option under `build.target` or as a dedicated `environments` preset (following the new Vite Environments API introduced in Vite 6):

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { cloudflareWorkersEnvironment } from '@vitejs/plugin-cloudflare' // new

export default defineConfig({
  environments: {
    worker: cloudflareWorkersEnvironment({
      entry: 'src/worker.ts',
      compatibilityDate: '2024-09-23',
    }),
  },
})
```

This would:
- Disable Node.js shims automatically
- Use `workerd`-compatible module resolution
- Emit a single-file ES module bundle (no dynamic import splitting)
- Handle `.wasm` imports via the Workers Wasm binding pattern

### Related

- Vite 6 Environments API: https://vitejs.dev/guide/api-environment
- Cloudflare Workers module syntax: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/migrate-to-module-workers/
- `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` is heading in this direction but a first-party integration would be ideal

Happy to contribute a plugin or RFC if the team is interested in discussing the direction.

closed.title: optimizeDeps.include accepts a project source file and pre-bundles it, but nothing ever resolves to it
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

Listing a project source file (not in `node_modules`) in `optimizeDeps.include` is accepted: the dep optimizer runs on it and writes the pre-bundle into `node_modules/.vite/deps`, and it shows up in `_metadata.json` under optimized. But no import ever resolves to it — the file keeps being served as source, module by module — and no warning is printed. The pre-bundle is simply dead output.

The reason looks structural: in `vite:resolve` (and in `vite:pre-alias`) the call to `tryOptimizedResolve` sits behind `if (bareImportRE.test(id))`, and `tryOptimizedResolve` matches the optimizer metadata ​by specifier string​, not by resolved file path. A relative import that resolves to the very file listed in include therefore can never hit the optimized dep.

What I'd like clarified: is accepting a source path in `optimizeDeps.include` intended (in which case relative imports resolving to it arguably ought to be redirected), or is it out of scope (in which case Vite could warn, the way it already warns for include entries it cannot resolve)?

The use case for this is that we have a "library" included in the project as ~ 100 source files. The library code won't change and doesn't need HMR etc support so it would be efficient to pre-bundle it. It is however not an npm package.

closed.title: `build.license` attributes the wrong version and omits license text for packages with nested `package.json` type markers
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

`build.license` resolves each bundled module to its package via
`findNearestMainPackageData`. For packages that ship a dual ESM/CJS build with a bare
type-marker `package.json` in a subdirectory, resolution stops at the marker instead of
the real package root. The emitted license file then reports `0.0.0` as the version and
carries no license text or SPDX identifier for those packages.

This matters more than a normal metadata glitch: the output of this option is an
attribution notice. A file that names a dependency with a fabricated version and no
license text does not discharge the notice clause it exists to satisfy, and it fails
silently — there is nothing in the output to indicate the entry is incomplete.

### Reproduction

Any package with this layout reproduces it. `socket.io-client` and its transitive deps
are a convenient case:

```
node_modules/engine.io-client/package.json              → name, version 6.6.3, license MIT, LICENSE file
node_modules/engine.io-client/build/esm/package.json    → {"name":"engine.io-client","type":"module","browser":{…}}
```

With `build.license` enabled and `socket.io-client` imported, the emitted file contains:

```
## @socket.io/component-emitter - 0.0.0     (actual: 3.1.2, MIT)
## engine.io-client - 0.0.0                 (actual: 6.6.3, MIT)
## engine.io-parser - 0.0.0                 (actual: 5.2.3, MIT)
## socket.io-client - 4.8.3                 (version correct; no identifier, no text)
```

`socket.io-client` differs because its own marker happens to include `version`.

### Root cause

`findNearestMainPackageData` recurses upward only while `name` is absent:

```js
function findNearestMainPackageData(basedir, packageCache) {
  const nearestPackage = findNearestPackageData(basedir, packageCache);
  return nearestPackage && (nearestPackage.data.name
    ? nearestPackage
    : findNearestMainPackageData(path.dirname(nearestPackage.dir), packageCache));
}
```

A type-marker manifest carrying `name` but no `version` satisfies that predicate, so it
is treated as the main package data. The license plugin then reads
`{ name, version = '0.0.0', license }` from the marker and looks for a license file in
the marker's directory, where there isn't one.

### Suggested fix

Requiring `version` as well as `name` before accepting a manifest as the main package
data would resolve it. If tightening the shared helper is undesirable — other callers may
legitimately want a name-only match — the license plugin could keep walking upward while
`version` is missing, or resolve the package root from the last `node_modules/` path
segment instead.

Either way it would be worth having the plugin surface incomplete entries rather than
emitting them, since the failure is otherwise invisible in the output.

Related precedent: #19324 handled the adjacent case of a `package.json` without `name`
reaching `resolveLibCssFilename`. This is the `name`-without-`version` variant, surfacing
in a different consumer.

### Environment

Observed on `vite@7.3.1` and on a Rolldown-based Vite 8 distribution; the plugin
implementation is identical in both. pnpm 10.11.1, Node 22, Linux.

closed.title: Windows: server.host 'localhost' binds IPv6 only; proxy to localhost:port fails with ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, a Vite dev server configured with `server.host: 'localhost'` can listen only on IPv6 (`[::1]:port`).

When another Vite app proxies to `http://localhost:port`, Node often connects via IPv4 (`127.0.0.1`), so proxy requests fail.

In the browser this often appears as:

`TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`

even though the target module path is valid.

### Reproduction

**Environment**
- OS: Windows 10/11 (build 26200)
- Node: v20.x
- Vite: 5.4.21
- Package manager: npm / pnpm

**Setup**

App A (target), `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    port: 5002,
    host: 'localhost',
  },
});
```

App B (proxy / hub), `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    port: 5000,
    proxy: {
      '/front-office': {
        target: 'http://localhost:5002',
        changeOrigin: true,
        ws: true,
      },
    },
  },
});
```

**Steps**
1. Start App A (`vite`, port 5002)
2. Start App B (`vite`, port 5000)
3. Open `http://localhost:5000/front-office/`
4. Navigate to a route with lazy / dynamic imports

**Observed**
- Hub / proxy logs:
  - `http proxy error ... AggregateError [ECONNREFUSED]`
  - `http proxy error ... AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT]`
- Browser:
  - `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:5000/front-office/@fs/.../index.ts`

**Network check on Windows**

```powershell
netstat -ano | findstr :5002
# LISTENING on [::1]:5002 (IPv6 only)

curl http://[::1]:5002/front-office/      # 200
curl http://127.0.0.1:5002/front-office/  # fails
```

### Expected behavior

Proxying to `http://localhost:5002` should work reliably on Windows when App A is running.

### Actual behavior

Proxy requests fail intermittently or consistently because App A is reachable on IPv6 but not IPv4.

### Workaround

Set the target app host to `0.0.0.0` (or `true`):

```ts
server: {
  port: 5002,
  host: '0.0.0.0',
}
```

After this:
- `127.0.0.1:5002` works
- hub proxy to `localhost:5002` works

### Why this matters

`server.host: 'localhost'` is a common setup. Monorepo setups with a hub app and multiple Vite apps behind a proxy are common, and this failure mode is hard to debug because the browser error points at module import paths, not networking.

### Suggested improvements

1. Document Windows localhost IPv4 / IPv6 behavior for `server.host`
2. Warn when dev server is IPv6-only but proxy / client uses `localhost`
3. Consider a safer default for Windows proxy / monorepo workflows

### Additional context

This is not an application code failure: production build succeeds, and direct access to the target port over IPv6 works before the workaround.

closed.title: Vite 8.2.x leaves CSS asset URLs stale after PostCSS transforms
closed.body:
### Describe the bug

_most of the issue is written by AI_

Vite 8.2.x can emit hashed CSS assets while leaving the original source-relative `url()` unchanged. The generated CSS then points at a source path that is not present beside the output CSS file.

The regression reproduces in two independent configurations:

1. Sass with `postcss-lightningcss`.
2. `@tailwindcss/vite` with an empty PostCSS configuration.

Both fixtures produce the expected asset URLs with Vite 8.1.5. With Vite 8.2.2, the asset files are still emitted but the CSS references stale relative URLs.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Razunter/vite-82-css-bug-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repo.
2. Install dependencies:

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

3. Run the four comparison builds:

   ```bash
   npm run build:postcss:8.1.5
   npm run build:postcss:8.2.2
   npm run build:tailwind:8.1.5
   npm run build:tailwind:8.2.2
   ```

4. Inspect the generated CSS files under the four `dist-*` directories.

Each script invokes its Vite version through `npx --yes`; the fixture manifest itself remains pinned to Vite 8.2.2.

### System Info

```shell
System:
  OS: Linux 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x64
  Environment: DDEV on WSL2
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.0
  npm: 11.16.0
Packages:
  vite: 8.2.2
  rolldown: 1.2.5
  @tailwindcss/vite: 4.3.3
  postcss-lightningcss: 1.1.1
  sass: 1.103.0
  tailwindcss: 4.3.3
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

The builds complete successfully; the failure is visible in the emitted CSS.

```text
Vite 8.1.5 / PostCSS:
  url(/assets/Roboto-Regular-BKwBj7lc.ttf)
  url(/vite-css-url-repro.webp)

Vite 8.2.2 / PostCSS:
  url(../fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf)
  url(/vite-css-url-repro.webp)

Vite 8.1.5 / Tailwind:
  url(/assets/vite-css-url-repro-HxSRdrt5.webp)
  url(/vite-css-url-repro.webp)

Vite 8.2.2 / Tailwind:
  url(../images/vite-css-url-repro.webp)
  url(/vite-css-url-repro.webp)
```
